reviews_content: Khao San Road is a must see by all who visits Bangkok! My wife being a Thai national, she wanted me to see it. She also loves "walking streets" as she calls them. This one is a little more wild than just a market. It is colored with massage parlors and bars, weed shops and a lot of foreigners. I don't think I saw more "Farang" in any other place than here. :D And the jumpoff jumps off when the sun goes down. It gets loud and more lively! Don't accept anything you don't really want, cause the locals are pretty aggressive in trying to push things on visitors. Going with kids after sundown is your choice, I do not recommend it. It is a fun place for adults. Get a massage, eat some crazy things like scorpions or huge spiders, get tanked and party or smoke a doobie and sit zoned out watch people walk by...whatever floats your boat. :) Khao San Road got you! || A place to visit if you’re in Bangkok mainly out of curiosity, just to see what it’s about. You’ll find plenty of bars, street food, souvenir shops and loud nightlife, all packed into a very busy area.  That said, beyond the atmosphere, there isn’t much that stands out. Most of the products sold feel low quality and mass-produced, clearly aimed at tourists. It can be fun for a quick walk-through, but it’s not a place I’d spend much time if you’re looking for something authentic or meaningful. || I spent New Year’s Eve on Khao San Road, and it was one of the busiest places I’ve ever been. The whole street was packed with people celebrating, loud music everywhere, and lots of lights and street food. It felt exciting and kind of chaotic at the same time.  Because it was so crowded, it was hard to move around and you definitely have to be patient and stay aware of your things. Still, the atmosphere was fun and the countdown was memorable. I’d recommend it if you like big crowds and a party vibe — just be prepared for noise and very little space. || Khao San Road: Your Must-Go Global Hub in Bangkok! Khao San Road in Bangkok is an absolutely essential stop for anyone traveling to Thailand—it's the world-famous, vibrant, and bustling backpacker mecca! This street truly comes alive from about 4 PM until the early hours. You'll find a massive array of open-air bars, lively pubs, diverse street food, and countless shops selling everything a traveler could need. The great news is that prices here are very reasonable and generally comparable to what you'd find elsewhere. While many services post clear prices, a friendly negotiation is still often recommended before you commit, just to be sure. If you plan to stay right on the main street, places like D&D Inn Khaosan offer good value and are often very reasonably priced, but remember to book in advance on major travel websites, as they fill up fast! The quality is perfectly suitable for the typical, adventurous traveler. Explore the Softer Side: Neighboring Streets Don't miss the charming, interconnected lanes surrounding Khao San! Areas like Thanon Ram Buttri Night Market and Ram Buttri Alley are stunning and also packed with great shops, restaurants, and bars. These streets offer a slightly more relaxed and gentle vibe than the main road, making them a perfect alternative if you prefer a less intense experience. Whether you're looking for an all-night party or a chill evening with a beer, Khao San Road and its neighboring streets are definitely a 'Must-Go' destination on your Thai adventure! || A good place to just vibe in. A place filled full witg tourist who want to party and have a good time. There are alot of bars and clubs located along with massage parlours. Foot Massages here ramge from 300 bhar per half hour. Beer in bars are around 130 bhar for a large Chang, Singha and Leo. There are many street vendors both to eat and shop. We also saw alot of hotels. Be careful, the street is really noisy for you to get a good sleep if you book it there. There are street vendors selling beers as well. 7/11 sells beers but not on restricted times. Its fun to just bar hop or sit on a bar and enjoy people dancing and just enjoying the vibe. Must experience if you habe time in Bangkok. Tip: Go late after 11 or 12. Its more lively. || Had never previously managed to visit Khaosan Road despite several visits to Bangkok.  We visited on a Monday and, despite its reputation for being a little bit tacky and massively crowded, it was actually a very pleasant, open, low-rise street. There are lots of useful shops on that street and nearby selling the predictable items such as luggage, T-shirts, trousers, shirts, etc. ( and many other interesting cafes and shops) , but the overall atmosphere was relaxed and friendly. There was no hassle at all, and it was genuinely pleasant just to be there.  Nearby is Rambuttri Road, another area often described as "spoiled" and “touristy.”  However this reputation is overplayed — both areas are still pleasant places to visit and just another very individual part of the myriad different zones and areas of this incredible City.  This area is very easy to get to if you take the hop-on, hop-off tourist boat and get off at the final stop, Phra Arthit Pier. From there it’s an easy three-minute walk: exit the pier, turn right, walk about 100 metres, then turn left. || I went last night (a Thursday night) around 22h00. This road has been closed off for markets and the festivities there. Similar to Bangla road in Phuket, but less extreme. It is quite busy; people everywhere, loud music in most of the restaurants, with a few half naked people dancing on tables on some restaurants, and a few showing their menus. Unlike Bangla, this one has a lot of market selling Thai food, finger food like spring rolls and pork on a stick, as well as fruits, clothes, bags, and passport covers. They even have stations to do massages and nails, which I did and was impressed. The interesting ones were the stalls with skinned crocodile where you could take a picture for 10 or 20 baht. Prices for food was reasonable, but for fashion items was high, even after negotiation! I wouldn't recommend shopping there. Just go for food stalls and the vibe. We left after midnight and it was still busy. It's good to go, but not nearly as exciting as the hype around it. || Excellent, lively all hours to be honest. 6.30am this morning people were still partying. Great people, great staff, great vibes everywhere. Only thing is, too many people hassle you to go in the bar/restaurant/clubs || This vibe is too good for night life. Beer z, night clubs , weed and laughing gas. This place is dope, you can be high as sky 😁. If you’re a back pack traveller, you’ll love this. Not recommended for children. I suggest not to carry any jewelry or high value items with you while here. Just travel with a summer outfit and always protect your belongings. Beers are cheap and always be aware of the surroundings. Do not drink any opened beer bottles and do not leave any drink unopened and finish the tab every time you order. If you follow this simple steps you won’t find any problems here. You could find crocodile meat , spiders and even centipedes here. Highly recommended for people who use weed. || We finished our Thailand adventure in Bangkok.  After we checked in, we grabbed a tuk tuk and headed to Khoa San Road.  Ken had been many years before, and was excited to share the experience.  We arrived fairly early (5:30pm)  there are many food stations, restaurants and bars.  Atmosphere:  Very welcoming, felt safe the entire time.  The local vendors seemed appreciative to have us there.  Our first stop was dinner, we ate in the back of the restaurant.  Prices were good for Thailand, food was also very good.  Like most places we stopped to eat the menu was very large and offered a wide variety of choices.  We walked around a bit and did some shopping.  As the sun was going down we stopped for a drink and sat by the laneway.   It was an authentic experience.   Many vendors came and offered their goods.  from scorpions on a stick to bracelets and other trinkets.  When we were heading out the atmosphere was transformed to party mode.  Lots of music, girls dancing on tables, owners trying to get us to enter clubs.    We still felt very safe, and if we were looking to party it would have been perfect!  Overall a great experience, and I recommend you add it to your stops.  Erin EnD Adventures

Good selection of fruit and vegetables as well as plenty of herbs and chillies to choose from. Meat and fish in abundance if your early as well as lots of other stalls selling everything you need for home cooking. Places to eat as well selling a variety of foods at decent prices. Definitely worth a walk around if your near. || Localized market in Bangkok, it's a great place to look around, taste local food and enjoy how the real people of Bangkok live. Most of the small vendors here don't speak much English yet they are really trying to communicate with foreigners and facilitate whatever they request for. This market open very early in the morning and if you walk around in the morning you will see many monks from nearby temples walking to college food from those who wants to do the Buddhist merit. || China town. Amazing food opens late. All sorts of street vendors. Chestnuts. Noodles. Seafood you can find what you want. Busy place || Her food was amazing.  The serving sizes. She is the sweetest person.  She comes with her own tables in chairs. This is the first real Thai food I had found. Staying in Chinatown.  😁  Great service and even better tasting Pad thai 👏 || Walking around you will find multiple vendors selling the same things; both for food and for clothes. You can find some deals here but you really have to sift through quite a few places first. Worth a visit if you're in the area and want to also visit Ram Buttri and Khao San roads. || Great market with plenty of options to have delicious breakfast. Don’t miss it! || a small market that has lot of good street food! they have fried tofu with sauce, bakes banana, and many more. a nice quick visit before heading to bigger market. || We came to this market because we thought maybe it would be cheaper and food would be better but that isn’t the case. We were charged much higher prices here as tourists than across the river by the palace. || Just some clothes stalls and one spice store || Great place to walk through if you’re looking for a bite to eat. Wouldn’t recommend it if you’re looking for clothes, they’re more aimed at an older Thai customer. The vibe on the street is friendly though :-)

My favourite destination for affordable fruits and home to my favourite sticky rice vendor! Enjoyed bargaining prices and tasting fruits of the season. I go here every time I’m in Bangkok. || Plenty of fruits in retails n wholesale. You can get huge jackfruit pack in 20 baht and 3 for 50 baht while night markets are selling with 60 baht per pack. Cheap n fresh vegetables n fruits || This is a nice market but I’ve been to way nicer ones in Bangkok so compared it’s just ok. I will say I bought probably the best BBQ Salt Fish at this market. It was super tasty. There is constant traffic moving as you explore so you always have to watch out for moving vehicles. I wouldn’t recommend it for families with kids. || Huge variety of well priced fruit and vegetable. We found stalls selling packed freshly made sticky rice. Brilliant! || This is a paradise for food enthusiasts on the hunt for fresh ingredients. Its vast selection of farm-fresh produce, aromatic herbs, and exotic spices will leave you amazed. Friendly local vendors and the market's lively ambiance make sourcing ingredients an enjoyable adventure. Get ready to elevate your culinary creations! Male sure to come past 10pm or even better-midnight. Activities will start winding down from about 3am. || next to mahanak market, at night all the hawkers open their pushcart stores. we had noodles, savoury coconut cake, skewers, some sort of Thai pancake, spicy salad fried chicken (my fav 🌷) & pad Thai from the nicest Thai auntie ❤️ … || Amazing variety of fresh fruits. Never seen so much of them before. Also tried durian here , bought dried shrimps and had a lot of fun😎 … || Finally place I was looking for. After visiting many other markets in Bangkok I felt pretty down due to the high prices of the fruit.  Then I've been here. Finally, the prices I was looking for. A lot of fruit in season for a great price. The quality was also good.  Definitely place to visit for all the fruit lover. Only cons is that they do not have the fruit out of season such as durian, mangosteam... so if you want these special fruit and it's not a season you will have to go to other markets which are highly overpriced. || Was looking for halal beef and there is one available at the back section of the market. No halal chicken, but various seafood choices. Fresh vegetables also available. Good to go over all || Great market, excellent price although more expensive than in south of Thailand. Highly recommend it if you want to shop like a local person not at tourist prices.

Local fruits and vegetables market. Good quality at reasonable wholesale price. || Fruit paradise!!! Loved this place!! Amazing fruit for very cheap!! || Extensive fruit market. The best quality fruits are more expensive than in Europe || best thai food i every try and also burmese food || Super market, a must for your trip in Bangkok. Don't miss it || Early morning is the right time to get the best out of the market... || Good fruit market nearby. || Good place to buy fruits

I come here often with my friends. It’s a great place to relax, they do a really good traditional massage. Everything is clean, the therapists are experienced, and they understand several languages, which is very convenient. I’m very happy with the service — thank you! || I came from Viet Nam and this is first time I have experience real Thai massage. The Technician name Tom have done very very good job. Im totally satisfy. It was everything my body needed after all that tiredness and sore muscles. You should try it too — highly recommend! You get a tea after too 💖 … || The environment and message is great, and the location is really excellent. While walking around Siam area, it’s a good spot to relax your body. || The best foot massage I have in bangkok. The staff are very friendly and professional. The recipient was very nice and polite. The service is great and worthy. || I am from the Philippines and on vacation here in Thailand. We’ve tried several massage spa but Thai Thai exceeded our expectations. The therapist was friendly and always asking if I am okay. I would highly recommend this spa to all my filipino friends. || Great experience! Did a foot massage and they hit the pressure points really well. We will come back again tomorrow to get a full body massage. Thank you Thai Thai flagship store! || Not disappointed by this Thai massage! Fair price and excellent massage. Thai massage rooms have wood dividers but they aren’t very private. I could hear the person next to me and it was distracting.  Still enjoyed my massage and the woman was excellent, strong and knowledgeable! Friendly note to other massage customers, no one wants to hear your groans while you’re getting a massage. || ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ This is my second time visiting this massage place. The therapist’s technique is amazing and truly relaxing. Highly recommend it to anyone visiting Bangkok! 💆🏻‍♀️✨ …

place_name: Pela Thai Massage : Siam Square soi6
reviews_content: Good reviews of Pela Massage don’t disappoint. It’s a great place for real relax. The quality of foot massage and body oil massage was really high. We will definitely come back to this place in the future and recommend it to our friends :). || I did a research for a massage place with consistent good reviews and it did not disappoint me.  I came with a very bad stiff and painful right arm. I told the counter staff my issue and she recommended me aromatherapy with Thai herbal ball (90mins) and assigned an experienced masseur for me. It was very very painful when she focused on my right arm but I can sense she put in effort to help me release the tension. Indeed no pain no gain. On the next day, my arm was much better, is not 100% but at least can move with lesser pain. || Very aesthetic place but I don’t think the massage was anything to shoutout about. Admittedly, this is very subjective and dependent on the masseuse. That said, this place seems to be heavily frequented by Chinese and Singaporeans due to the Google reviews so the recep area was definitely chaotic. Definitely suggest to consider other massage places nearby since there are loads of them within walking distance! || The massage place is really good. I had a shoulder and back massage which was super nice. Besides that they did my hands and head too. Very clean and the people are extremely polite. || A friend recommended this place, and it truly exceeded expectations. I visit many of the well‑known massage brands in Bangkok, and this experience was easily one of the best. Professional, relaxing, and genuinely impressive. Highly recommended. || Sooooo comfortable!! Also very clean and peaceful atmosphere, a bit Japanese style. Very authentic Thai massage!! Must try 90 mins, completely relaxed || A beautifully run Thai spa that delivers pure reset energy. The ambience flows with calm, the therapists work with skill and intention, and every treatment feels thoughtfully crafted. A consistently soothing, rejuvenating experience worth returning to. || Very clean, comfortable place. Attentive on the privacy of the client. The reception was very friendly and able to promote the package in details. The masseure apply the right pressure and very professional. Overall great service. || This was my first time using the service. The staff were polite and spoke kindly upon arrival. When I began the service and entered the private massage room, I immediately noticed a musty smell. I initially thought the odor would improve after the air conditioner had been running for a while, but it seemed that the smell was coming from the mattress itself. In addition, the air conditioner was positioned directly above my head, which made breathing quite uncomfortable during the session.  Regarding the massage, the service did not meet my expectations. I am someone who regularly receives massages, but this was my first time visiting this branch. The first therapist appeared to be attentive and used strong pressure, but lacked proper technique, which caused discomfort. As a result, I requested to change to another therapist. The second therapist provided better massage technique; however, their hands were constantly wet due to sweating, which made me feel uncomfortable and concerned about cleanliness, as it felt sticky and unhygienic.  After the massage, I asked the staff whether I could take a shower, but I was informed that Thai massage does not include shower facilities, so this service was not available.  As a Thai person who is familiar with traditional massage standards, I would not recommend this place to local customers. It seems the service may be more oriented toward foreign visitors rather than meeting the expectations of locals.  Overall, the experience was disappointing, and I do not think I will return. || I left feeling refreshed and deeply relaxed. I would definitely recommend Pela Thai Massage for anyone looking for a rejuvenating massage. Thank you for the wonderful service!

Had a really good experience here! The service was excellent, the atmosphere was relaxing and clean, and the massage technique was great. I also got a discount before 5pm. Will definitely come again! || I had an amazing experience at Nature Thai Massage! I got the Aromatherapy Office Syndrome treatment and absolutely loved it. The massage was both relaxing and effective.  The atmosphere was peaceful and clean, with private rooms that made the whole experience even more comfortable and calming. The staff were professional and welcoming. I highly recommend this place if you’re looking to truly unwind and relieve muscle tension || The shop is easy to access and quite convenient for travelers. However, my experience was a bit underwhelming — the massage lacked skill, the towels had an unpleasant smell, and the overall environment was just average. I hope the business takes customer feedback seriously and continues to improve. || Pj jum is very strong I like her massage so good❤️❤️❤️ Thankyou very much I feel refreshed 🥰 … || 1) Go in the afternoon for happy hour 20% discount. The 90 mins package is worth it- so nice to relax in between shopping.  2) The foot massage on chairs is on the ground level and the individual mats for thai/body massage is on the 2nd and 3rd floor.  They are located very near the bts and siam malls so it is convenient to get to. || Honestly, both JUM and FSON offer amazing massage experiences. Their staff are really professional and know exactly how to make you feel relaxed. The atmosphere is calm and clean, and the massage itself is super soothing. I left feeling lighter and refreshed. I highly recommended👍🏼 … || I recently had an unforgettable massage experience with a friend, thanks to a local recommendation! The place was a hidden gem suggested by my local friend, and it truly exceeded my expectations. The therapist was incredibly kind and professional, using expert techniques to relieve all the tension in my muscles. I felt completely refreshed and recharged afterward – like all the fatigue just melted away. I’d definitely love to go back again next time! || Worst massage ever!! Did the 60 minute foot massage and she barely even touched my feet, just kept pressing her hands on my legs!!!! No pressure at all. Therapist was disinterested. It’s a foot massage lady, not a leg massage.  Typical place that looks good from the outside and fails to deliver a good service. Tourist trap! Never going back, I’ll be sticking to my other places which are also better priced. || I had a wonderful first time experience here at Nature Thai! The masseuses here are very skilled and meticulous in their services. I felt immediate relief after the massage, highly recommend trying their Aroma Stress Release program + Hot Herbal Compress! K’Mor Rin did an excellent work and I will be back here again :)) || This was my first Thai massage and I absolutely loved it! I will definitely be back and would love to bring my friends and family here :)

I can see why this place is near perfect score. The prices are a bit higher but it’s worth the price tag. The spa is spotless. You can really tell how thats really important for them. Booked a 90 min Thai massage. Booking was easy. I did it via WhatsApp or you can just call from WhatsApp as well. Masseuse was Mai. I feel like she is the black belt if Thai massages. I asked for medium strength but I was in agony all throughout. I wonder what hard pressure feels like. There’s the type of people who likes 0 strength and there’s people like me, who feels like a massage should be painful for it yo be effective. Mai has moves I’ve never seen before and I’ve had my fair share of massages. Arm rolling on your abs? That felt oddly weird and I’m glad I wasn’t full of food. It almost felt like she wanted me to wave the white flag. And I almost did but I preservere. And the more I show mercy, the more she squeezed. It was a battle of will. Anyway, massage was great for me. Some will not like it but anyone can do a light massage. It’s the special ones that can apply this much pressure for straight 90 mins. || we go in so thai spa with my wife for a so thai luxury package (4h) for couples, after a night in the bus, waiting for check-in in our hotels. We went there with MRT which is a bit far ~10min walk by foot. Walk is easy as you can go in small streets without cars, but better if not too hot (we have been lucky on that). Booking was easy with website and all their means of communication, got an answer very fast. The place is very nice and you are welcomed with a refreshing cup or cold tea. Do not hesitate to tell your preferences at the reception, and if you pain somewhere so they can be careful. We then followed our host on another floor to go to our room (after cleaning our feet) , that was really nice, beautiful and soothing, and could get our massages together in this room (we both made different choices according to our tastes included in the package). A break was planned during the treatment with a shower and a few treats, all very good! I asked for a strong thai massage and wasnt disappointed, but you should only chose it if you like it strong :) Got out of this place fully refreshed and rested even after a (short) night sleeping in the bus from the north. Will go again without a doubt next time in Thailand. Highly recommend. || I came to the So Thai Spa today and enjoyed the So Thai Nirvana 5 hour package. Tae was absolutely wonderful. She was very attentive and friendly, and her skills were very nice. The pressure was just right and I felt so relaxed. I even fell asleep many times because of how comfortable it was. Definitely 5 hours well spent. The snacks and refreshments were also nice.  Next time I come to Bangkok, this is definitely the place to feel relaxed and get a nice massage. Definitely feeling pampered! || Incredible experience! Booked the couples So Thai Luxury which was such a good price for foot massage, body scrub, massage, and facial. Very clean, relaxing, incredible outdoor shower, snacks, and of course the massage therapists were 10/10!! If you're looking for a reputable, high end spa with really good prices - this is the place to go! || Visited the spa with my father after a long day of touristing. Took the three hour package and throughly enjoyed the service. We had Poo and On as our masseuses. They were amazing and very hospitable. Would definitely recommend || Excellent from every perspective! Clean, quiet and professional.They gave me an ice tea while I was waiting to prepare my room (delicious) and afterwards they offer a hot tea as well. Before the massage they asked me about preferred areas to massage or not and the pressure level I want. My masseuse “King” was very friendly and knowledgeable, respected all my requests and gave me an amazing and relaxing massage. They even scrub your feet before the massage. I’m definitely coming back. Reasonable prices. I did the hot stone massage and I definitely recommend it! || I came to so Thai Spa im 2024 and did the 4 hour spa package.  I loved it so much I had to bring my husband this time.  We got the 4 hour spa package which started with a welcome drink, foot clean, foot & leg massage, full body scrub, beautiful shower, light refreshments, full body massage and herbal ball compress. Absolute bliss, highly recommend 😁 || Absolutely amazing massage, beautiful spa and lovely people. Greeted with delicious tea and such a peaceful and calming environment. We had two-hour massages and I would not have wanted to spend a moment less. I hope to enjoy a four-hour experience on my next visit. Enjoy! || I had an amazing experience at So Thai Spa. Sun was an amazing massage therapist. She applied the right amount of pressure and it felt like she tuned into what my muscles needed. I left feeling more relaxed, with less muscle tightness and no tension. I would highly recommend. I will be returning.  My service was the So Thai Pleasure Spa package. || If I could give this place 10 stars I would!!!!! It was a fantastic experience. I loved EVERY minute of it. I don’t think I’ve ever felt this great after a massage before. Bo and Lily were both amazing masseuses and took care of my partner and I every minute that we were here. RUN don’t walk at this opportunity to treat yourself/loved one if you’re in the Bangkok area!!! You won’t regret it. 🤭

I was in the area and decided to see if I could get a massage before my seafood buffet dinner. It was very busy when I walked in but luckily I was able to get my Thai massage with herbal press for 90 mins (750 bhat cash only). The receptionist was very friendly and asked if I'd like to go to the toilet first. I thought that was very considerate - better than other more expensive massage places I've been.  The masseur was excellent - probably my best thai massage so far. I was very impressed. The herbal press smelled lovely but it was occasionally too hot on the skin. Overall, the massage had a great combination of proper work out (Thai bit) and relaxation (herbal press).  However, the masseur finished 7 mins earlier. Nevertheless, I was surprised that there was a nice treat waiting for me. The lovely frensh coconut water with tea and biscuit. Really love the quenching coconut water - it was exactly what I needed!  I will be back again! Highly recommend! || We visited this shop last night on the strength of the reviews. As in every other shop, it is hit and miss.  No guaranteed good massage at all.  We all had a full body hour massage and each one had a different experience.  All of us concur our experience from a shop that is not too far is better.  This shop don’t have hawker’s trying to grab every passers by.  Won’t come back, i’m afraid but still massive thank you to the polite staff. || I had the best experience with a friendly, English-speaking masseuse named Aom 😊😊, highly look-up for her. The price was affordable, and the quality of the massage was excellent. We were even welcomed with a cold coconut water, which was such a nice touch! Highly recommended for anyone who’s had a long day of walking and shopping. … || Been to Bangkok countless times, and with City of Massage located at such a prominent location, I can’t believe I’ve been missing out all this while. Why didn’t I patronize this place on my past trips here? City of Massage offers one of the best massages I’ve ever had in Bangkok!  We walked in at 10:30pm and it was already packed.  It is a clear sign of how popular it is. Even with a 35-minute wait, it was completely worth it. From the moment my therapist began the 90-minute Head-to-Toe massage I chose, I could tell that this place has some standard in place.  Im typing this review while doing the massage. The massage is incredible! My therapist - Jab was skilled, knowing exactly how to target the pressure points and ease away all the tension, especially those knots I had on my shoulder for the longest time. It was honestly one of the best massages I’ve ever experienced, and I can’t recommend City of Massage highly enough!  Setback - The salon is located right next to the main road hence it can be disturbing.  Nevertheless, the good massage can make up for this!! || After a long, exhausting day, I stumbled upon this place using Google Maps, and I am so grateful for my decision! Pok is incredibly professional and kind. I drifted off to a peaceful slumber during the massage session. Following a rejuvenating 60-minute foot massage, my fatigue melted away, leaving me ready to hit the shops once more! I highly recommend this place—it's truly a gem and offers great value for money! || I have been twice it really depends which massage you pick. In the busy timings they would say they cannot accommodate you if you pick the package which costs less then 1000 bath. I was very disappointed because at first visit I had the best experience. The lady wasn’t helpful and she didn’t want to book my later visit she said come and try but what if’s not available I wouldn’t waste the time coming if I am not sure if you could accommodate me. The place is clean and new. Attaching photos from my visit. Enjoy || Super affordable massage with great therapist. My therapist Top was friendly and really skillful. Recommended to come if you're around this area. The environment was clean and comfy too || A super frustrating and disappointing experience at this so called highly rated massage place. Firstly I tried to email and got no response, so did asking the hotel to call. I checked on their website and realized they don't do online or call booking and has to be done on-site so fine I visited when the shop opened, followed the instructions on the website wanted to go and make a reservation for the afternoon. So I wanted to do an hour foot and an hour body. I asked to make a reservation for 3pm and the person at the counter told me I can't make reservation. How ridiculous it is they totally don't follow the booking procedure on the website! The person (I don't know the gender) said if I wanted to do at 3pm I should walk in at 3. So I said fine I want to do both the foot and the body right now and she said oh I can only do foot now no body. Don't understand what the person meant by no body massage until past 2pm. So I went for walk and lunch and came back at 3 and then I said I wanted to do foot and body and was told only foot available no body massage for the rest of the day. I couldn't understand the logic whether it was due to limited beds or masseurs cause I don't see any beds and I saw so many masseurs walking around. Then I asked for male masseur but was told none available and assigned a female one for me. In the end I chose to do a foot massage which was mediocre and while massaging there were just like 3-4 male masseurs just walking around and the next person came in just got assigned a male masseur. Very bad customer service and the procedures don't even follow what they stipulated on the website total waste of time. So angry and dissatisfied I just finished the massage and looked for another massage place nearby to do my body massage. The price here is also not considered cheap, take a walk around the ones nearby and they are cheaper. || Been there couple days ago took relaxing massage with my gf, they don't negotiate, prices are significantly higher compared to rest of bangkok.  Rather than using their hands they use their elbows making process quite painful despite massage should have been relaxing.  Massage therapists are moody and they push you to buy 90 min massage therapy for the next day.  Massage rooms are very cold and not the cleanest place to be. Tucked away from the chaos of Bangkok’s streets, the Museum of Bangkok is a refreshing step back in time. Walking through the exhibits feels like peeling back layers of the city’s story, from its early days to the vibrant metropolis it is today. The displays are easy to follow, thoughtfully curated, and give real context to how locals lived, worked, and adapted as the city grew. It’s a great break from temples and markets, especially if you enjoy understanding the why behind a place. Calm, informative, and surprisingly engaging—well worth adding to your Bangkok itinerary. || The Bangkok National Museum is a peaceful and culturally important place to visit, especially if you want to learn more about Thailand’s history, traditional art, and royal heritage. The museum complex is spacious, the buildings themselves are beautiful, and the exhibits give you a nice overview of Thai culture, religion, and past civilizations. It’s a quiet break from Bangkok’s chaos and a good spot for anyone who enjoys museums.  However, it’s worth mentioning that the collection is not as rich or extensive as you might expect from a “national museum.” Some sections feel a bit limited, and a few areas could use more modern presentation or detailed explanations. If you’ve visited larger national museums around the world, this one may feel more modest in comparison. || First the shortcomings. The Museum  is not for person with disabilities, even a senior citizen has to careful while climbing 2nd floor.Many floor tiles are uneven. There are no indicators regarding Exit. I got lost and spent 10 minutes to exit. Only room numbers are mentioned. Finally lighting was so poor that it was not possible to read the information cards. Now the positive side many clean hygienic  toilets well maintained. The the collection from earlier empires well documented both in Thai and English. Number of school children were seeing   the collection. Lots of people were taking interest, reading the notes and photography  the works. Different period works were duly arranged and important information  about them provided. Works from Srilanka, India (Pala, Gupta and Sarnatha Mathura period), Java, Afghanistan, Indonesia,Laos, Khmer, Vazrayana (Chines influence) were well depicted. Two cafeteria one which serves Thai cuisine and the coffee shop next to ticket office. There is a well stocked artistic works in Museum souvenir shop. Some renovation is ongoing so not all could be accessed. But thanks for such rich Thai heritage in which my country India,  Buddhist and Hindu philosophy and religion  have kindred contribution. Buddha Namah! || An iconic tourist attraction in Bangkok and also one of the most beautiful places I’ve seen in Thailand. Put on nice socks because you will have to take your shoes off to enter some rooms like in many places in Thailand. As it is a very touristic place, unless you go first thing in the morning, it will be crowded so don’t expect to take pictures with nobody in them. Also bring a bottle of water because the place is huge. However the architecture with so many different styles is very impressive and the atmosphere amazing. The collection of artwork is impressive and you can learn a lot about the history of the country. So beautiful. I highly recommend || Lovely museum with loads of great exhibits. I would recommend to focus on buildings 4 and 5 (the ones at the far end of the compound) since those provide a comprehensive overview of local history history, starting at prehistoric times and ending in the 19th/20th century. The exhibits' arrangement might seem a bit dated, but the nice and tranquil atmosphere even on an otherwise busy Friday afternoon makes up for that. || Please be advised, video recording not encouraged. 240baht for foreigner. Flow is great, we went in the order of 1, 4 (golden boy), 5 and finally 6. Buddhism artifacts from various countries. Art styles from Lanna to recent Rattanakosin. Spent around 3hours or so. There's a cafe inside with not great food or drinks but it'll do the job if you're hungry.  Some of the buildings are more modern and have elevators but some of the buildings are older and would be harder for wheelchair users ♿️ || Historic art is exhibited at this museum. Very rare items of Thai history & culture. Lot of information on each art piece. I learn a lot about my own country here. Very beautifully displayed. || It's a really big museum with a lot to see, so be sure to plan plenty of time for visiting it. It's great to see it during mid day, when the sun is high and it gets too hot for comfort to walk outside. The entrance has a free baggage room, to make the visit to the musuem more enjoyable.

Some reviews say the exhibition is for young people, but I think it's a well curated museum to let you consider what it means to be Thai, and the evolution of the different identities of the people here. It may be simple for some people, but I thought the interactive, fun and casual exhibits help make it more immersive for you to consider the Thai identity. Also, while the exhibit may seem fun, I think it does provide some thought-provoking questions—we may think of the Thai identity as static, but this exhibition invites you to consider to different identities, and it is also willing to ask an honest question—what does it really mean to be Thai? And also, what are the origins of symbols of Thai identity and have we thought to question them? || We went here on Tuesday, just a few tourists and primary students. The admission fee is 100THB, which is reasonable for the experience offered, though I think it might be worth spending money and time on the nesrby National Museum Bangkok than this because I can assure that place will wow you. || Perfect!
