I spent about two really nice hours here. The house is beautiful, and the lush garden a calm, shady place.  I joined an English-speaking guided tour, which was easy to follow and very informative. In about 40 minutes, the guide gave us all a great overview and shared interesting background about the place.  I also had plenty of time to walk around the garden and explore a few of the other buildings on my own, both before and after the tour.  There’s a shop with lovely silk items, though many are on the expensive side. The restaurant is a nice extra and a good spot to take a break during your visit. || Jim Thompson House Museum is one of the most fascinating and rewarding cultural experiences in Bangkok. Tucked away in a surprisingly quiet and green area of the city, the museum offers a sharp contrast to the surrounding urban energy. From the moment you enter, you feel transported into a different time and atmosphere, calm, elegant, and deeply rooted in Thai culture. The traditional teak houses are beautifully preserved and thoughtfully arranged, showcasing an impressive collection of Asian art, antiques, and architectural details. Every room tells a story, not only about Thai craftsmanship and aesthetics, but also about Jim Thompson himself, his vision, his passion for art, and the mystery surrounding his life. The guided tour is highly recommended. Informative, well structured, and engaging, it adds real depth and context to what you are seeing, turning the visit into a meaningful cultural journey rather than a simple walk-through. The gardens are equally charming, lush, peaceful, and perfectly integrated into the experience, making the visit feel relaxed and immersive. Overall, the Jim Thompson House Museum is a must-visit for anyone interested in Thai history, architecture, and culture. Elegant, authentic, and thoughtfully curated, it offers a rare glimpse into a refined side of Bangkok that is both inspiring and memorable. || Quite an interesting place. TBH, I wasn’t planning on visiting the Jim Thompson House Museum; however a friend had programmed it into our itinerary. The guided tour of the house was very interesting, and the design and structure of the house (which contains pieces assembled from six other houses) was very impressive. Also the artefacts contained within were simply stunning. It appears that Jim Thompson and his incredible work to promote Thai silk worldwide left an indelible mark on Thailand. || The restaurant at The Jim Thompson House is truly exceptional — a perfect blend of elegance, Thai charm, and warm hospitality. After exploring the historic teak houses and beautiful gardens, dining here feels like the perfect continuation of the experience.  The atmosphere is refined yet relaxing, with thoughtful design touches that make the space feel both sophisticated and inviting. The food is beautifully presented, full of authentic Thai flavors, and the drinks — especially the cocktails — are outstanding.  What really elevates the experience is the service. Gam, Fon, and Arm were absolutely wonderful: friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. They made the entire visit feel personal and memorable.  Whether you’re visiting the museum or simply looking for a classy spot to enjoy Thai cuisine, this restaurant is a true Bangkok gem. Highly recommended! || Spent a lovely hour and a half here. Easy to get to via the canal taxi boats. Beautiful house and lush garden. Cool on a hot afternoon. Bags go in a free locker before tour starts. Shoes on for part of tour and off for the house. We went on one of the English speaking tours. Our guide was clear and informative. It took 45 minutes in which she gave a good overview. We had time to take photos in each space. We then spent another 30+ minutes exploring the garden and a couple of buildings on our own after the tour. There is a shop with beautiful silk products, but most things a bit out of our price range! We popped into the Art Exhibition too. A lovely way to spend an afternoon. . || We thoroughly enjoyed our visit to the Jim Thompson House. Please be advised that you can enter the house only as part of a tour. English lead tours should be around every half an hour and last the same time. Our tour guide was amazing. She was very knowledgeable and witty. Not only was she able to answer any questions she also provided some memorable puns with professional delivery. 🙏🙏🙏 We also enjoyed visiting the shop and would have loved to buy more since the prices are less than half compared to European outlets. || I was surprised just how interesting the tour was - they managed to fit a lot into 45 minutes without it ever feeling rushed. The focus was equal parts Jim Thompson's life story and the history of Thai culture and architecture. Would recommend booking ahead. || The Jim Thompson House is an absolute must-visit in Bangkok — especially for anyone who loves design, architecture, or history. Every corner is visually stunning, from the beautifully preserved traditional Thai teak houses to the lush tropical gardens that surround them.  The restaurant and café are also wonderful — elegant, relaxing, and a perfect spot to unwind after touring the house. The food and drinks are excellent, with the same thoughtful design touches that make the entire experience feel special.  A true Bangkok gem that blends art, culture, and craftsmanship. Highly recommend! || Interesting man and a nice museum if you are into interiors and architecture. The arts centre next door is a very interesting design. It is quite hot, so dress appropriately. The tour is included in the entry fee and was well coordinated and interesting. || I visited the museum in 2019 and fell in love with this hidden treasure in the heart of Bangkok. I visited again to see this place again and I was still amazed at how beautiful and peaceful this place is. I would definitely recommend the visit, and I would personally go with the flow in terms of tour times. It’s a place where you can sit and relax until your tour time. It’s been 7 years since I’ve been and I’ll definitely visit again on my next trip to Bangkok.

I love coming here each time I am back in Bangkok. An oasis of calm away from the hustle and bustle of Bangkok. Entrance is free except for special events. Charges for concerts and plays will vary. Exhibitions are subject to change. Check the website to see the current exhibitions. Bangkok Art and Culture Centre is connected to National Stadium BTS Station. A very quick walk. Alternatively, if you are in the Siam district and shopping, you can walk from there. Walk through Siam Discovery and you will see the Bangkok Art and Culture Centre opposite. Beautiful building. Apart from the art, the building also houses a variety of shops offering products and décor styles with an artistic touch, unique souvenirs, decorative accessories, and stationery, along with educational centres. You can also get a bite to eat or a beverage as well if you like. Would highly recommend if you are an art lover! || Bangkok Art and Culture Centre (BACC) is located in the heart of the Siam area. It is very easy to reach—just a short walk across the Skywalk from Siam Discovery. The building’s exterior is architecturally stunning and very photogenic.  Entrance to the museum is completely free, which makes it a very popular destination, so it can get quite crowded with tourists. It's a fantastic place to explore local art and culture without any admission fee. Definitely worth a visit!  #BACC #BangkokArt #SiamArea #BangkokMuseum #FreeThingsToDo #ThailandTravel #ArtCulture || Even if you don't love art the building itself is quiet impressive inside. The spaces are designed to really emphasize negative space.  Although not all of the displays will be to everyones taste, the gallery has contemporary and large art displays on the upper floors.  Great place to spend a couple hours absorbing the meaning behind the pieces. || I visited on a weekday. Not crowded at all. Amazing exhibitions, thought invoking and beautiful space. Took the BTS to get to Bangkok Art and Culture Center which was super easy to navigate as you can enter right from the platform basically. Highly recommend others to come here and then you can enjoy shopping at Siam Paragon, Siam Square, and MBK center. || If you have extra time in Bangkok, BACC is definitely worth a visit. This was my second time here, and it’s always exciting because the exhibitions change every month, so there’s something new to experience each visit. The entrance is free, and you’ll find a wide variety of art, culture, and history beautifully showcased. A very inspiring and enriching place — highly recommended! || Amazing architecture and well curated exhibits. Lucky to have caught the exhibit by Chatchai Puipia. There were staff who would explain the artworks and curation. Would recommend for those who are art enthusiasts. || It’s free to enter the building. There is a walkway to skywalk/National stadium station.  I enjoyed walking around not only in the unique exhibits but also the shops. I found a really nice leather + wood bag but I chickened out from buying lol. But there were so many creative items to choose from from different shops.  I also liked the interactive exhibit on Letting Go. || Beautiful architecture with spacious exhibition halls featuring unique and interesting artworks. A great place to explore contemporary art. Free admission and definitely worth a visit. || The Bangkok Art & Culture Centre building is very beautiful from the outside and impressive inside. That's the only good part.  Honestly, I found most of the exhibits pretty boring. But the worst part was on the last floor. There were literally photos of completely naked people, and they call this art? I was shocked and disgusted.  If you don't want to see nude pictures, I would avoid this place. It's a shame that such a beautiful building is filled with such disgusting and offensive content. Not my kind of art at all. || Visited there several months ago and this is definitely one of the best art compounds in Bangkok! The complex encompasses a couple of art exhibitions in different floors. Each exhibition has its own character and uniqueness. What is best about the whole experience is it is free of charge, which is great since most museums require entrance tickets. The center is well connected to the major malls around Siam BTS station such as MBK and Siam Discovery.

Good to spend time when vacation. Short experience but OK. Actually feel empty on weekeday, kind of spooky haha.  8/10 || Madam Tussauds was a really amazing place to visit. There were such a wide variety of stars, including our personal favorites. There were lots of photo opportunities with your favorite star. Lovely mix of Hollywood,  bollywood, sporting and cultural star. I enjoyed the interactive displays that allowed you to play a match. Loved the dress up costumes as well. My favorite was Einstein. The realistic,almost human like stars felt out of this world. If you are in Bangkok you can't afford to miss this! || Very detailed sculptures and you can touch them/be close to them for photos (more stable and not like the scam that is Mother's Wax Museum at Kolkata). Although I would recommend to keep a safe distance to avoid high penalties in case of unfortunate events as penalties are quite high in Bangkok (at least 5000 THB). || Jiancha at Siam discovery is the first store that I tried Jiancha. The seatings are interesting. The queue is typically not too long but sometimes could be crowded. But they are quite consistent and the tea here is great. || My wife and I made this in a combo ticket with the aquarium. It is a fun place for great photos. It is definitely worth it in combo with aquarium. || As someone who has spent years exploring attractions around the world, I've learned that some places are perfect for fun and photos. Madame Tussauds in Bangkok is a great example of this.  It’s located on the 4th floor of the Siam Discovery Center. Finding it can be a bit tricky, but it's worth the effort. Once you enter, you're welcomed by an incredible collection of wax figures. They look amazing, and the whole experience invites you to take photos with your favorite celebrities, historical figures, and movie characters. It's a fantastic day out, especially if you’re with friends or family and want to make some fun memories.  While it's a great place for photos, you can also learn a lot here. Each figure has a small sign detailing its history. So, if you feel like it, you can read up and get to know the people you're “meeting.”  A useful tip for visiting is to plan ahead. I heard that tickets can be purchased on Trip.com for about $17 AUD, which is a great price for the experience. This shows that a little planning can save you money and enhance your day.  Overall, Madame Tussauds is a must-visit for a fun, photo-filled day. Just remember to bring a little extra cash for your tickets online beforehand! || So good to see world-famous leaders, celebrities, and sports stars all in one place. The statues are astonishing — I wonder how they made them so perfect. It’s a small but great place to visit in Bangkok. || Madame Tussauds Bangkok, situated inside Siam Discovery in the city center, is a fun and engaging attraction for those eager to see wax figures of their favorite celebrities. The museum is divided into several themed sections like Red Carpet, Music, Film, World Leaders, Art & Science, and more. You'll find everything from movie stars and athletes to influential personalities from history, all crafted with impressive realism. Visitors can take pictures and interact with the displays, making it feel like a close-up encounter with famous figures.  The layout is user-friendly, with each zone clearly marked, allowing for a relaxed and enjoyable visit. However, it can get a bit crowded during busy hours, so there might be short waits to take photos with some of the most popular statues.  Admission prices are fair, and being located in Siam Discovery means it’s easy to reach if you're exploring the nearby shopping area. Also, keep an eye out for bundled ticket offers with SEA LIFE Bangkok to save more.  Whether you’re into movies, sports, politics, or science, Madame Tussauds Bangkok has something for every interest. It’s a worthwhile stop for both tourists and locals looking for a unique and entertaining experience. || Fun and interactive experience at Madame Tussauds Bangkok! We had a fantastic time visiting Madame Tussauds in Bangkok. The wax figures are incredibly realistic and well-crafted — it’s amazing how lifelike they look! There are plenty of popular celebrities, cultural icons, and themed sections that make the whole visit entertaining.  The interactive exhibits and photo opportunities are a highlight — perfect for both adults and kids who want to snap fun pictures with their favorite stars. The staff were friendly and helpful, and the venue felt clean and well organized.  Highly recommended for families, friends, and anyone who loves unique experiences! 🕺📸⭐️ || Madame Tussauds Bangkok, located in the heart of the city at Siam Discovery, is an exciting place to visit for anyone looking to meet their favorite celebrities in wax form. The museum offers a variety of themed zones, such as Red Carpet, Music, Film, Leaders, Art & Science, and more. From actors and athletes to historical figures, the place is full of lifelike wax figures that allow you to interact with them, take photos, and feel as if you’re standing next to a famous person.  The venue is well-organized, with clear sections for different celebrity categories, making it fun to explore at your own pace. While the experience is quite enjoyable, it does get busy, especially during peak tourist hours, so expect a bit of a wait to take photos with some of the more popular figures. Ticket prices are reasonable, and the venue is located in Siam Discovery, which makes it easy to access if you're already exploring the shopping district.  Whether you're a fan of Hollywood, sports, or history, Madame Tussauds Bangkok offers something for everyone, making it a must-visit spot for tourists and locals alike. Don’t forget to check out the promotions for combination tickets with SEA LIFE Bangkok for even better value. || Thank you so much for your thoughtful review. We're glad to hear you had a great time exploring the different zones and meeting your favorite wax figures. It's wonderful to know you enjoyed the interactive experience and convenient location. We appreciate your tips for future visitors and hope to welcome you back again soon.

Fantastic place to learn about the history of Bang Rak and Thailand in general. The museum consists of three beautiful houses set in a peaceful garden, each showcasing different aspects of traditional Bangkokian life in the mid-20th century.  The keepers at each house are incredibly kind and welcoming. They go out of their way to explain the background of each building and the history of the items on display.  The site features three beautifully preserved houses. One highlights the lifestyle of the original family, while others include interesting exhibits like a former medical practice and historical items from the World War II era.  Entry is free, though it is highly advisable to leave a donation to help with the maintenance and preservation of these heritage buildings. || This is a great little place to travel back in time for a moment. The house itself is beautiful and remarkably well-preserved for a home built almost 100 years ago, filled with many artifacts from the era. I especially loved the volunteer 'aunties' who went out of their way to teach us about the house and the family's history. The whole tour only took about 25 minutes and it was completely free, which is an amazing act of kindness from the family to open their home to the public. Highly recommended! || It's really worth coming here to visit, to take a look at how people lived in the early 1900s in Bangkok. It's nice to take a walk in the house and feel what it's like, and it items in the house have been maintained as they were. It's free to visit this museum and it's currently being maintained by the government. || I loved the visit to this house. Entrance is free. Quite oasi in the middle of chaos. 😅 Everything is well preserved. The descriptions are not well written and sometimes difficult to understand. I didn’t like the fact that the stuff was taking pictures and maybe video of me and other visitors without asking for permission. || It's free. It's something to do. A family home where the father was a doctor and some connection with royalty. From the World War II era through the 70s. The staff are nice. They'll take photos of you while you browse. || Staffed by volunteers, free entry. Very beautiful gardens and three houses to check out. The third one is air-conditioned, so if you need a break, that is a great place to stop.  If you like museums and enjoy seeing technology, history, architectural history, and how life used to be, it is a great place to visit.  If you are middle-aged like me, you will probably see a lot of things that are close to your childhood, from your childhood, or at least the predecessor of something you grew up with.  Really glad I walked here. || A cool museum free of charge allows you to see how Thai people used to live. There is air con in one of the buildings. Beware of the wooden stairs as they may get slippery. || You probably get a good insight of how the good old days in Bangkok was then, looking at the exhibits here. Well maintained and kept. Friendly and welcoming staff. || We had read about this museum and planned to visit but the day we chose turned out to be Chulalongkorn Day and AI was telling us it would be closed. Lucky that we ignored AI and still went there because not only was it open but it was free and lovely volunteer staff took time to show us around and explain things. Museum is made up of 3 old houses and they contain a lot of furniture, photos and household items relating to the former owners. A fascinating insight into life in Bangkok for middle - upper class people last century. || This remarkable "hidden gem" survives Bangkok rapid development, with an unassuming nature that the public mighg pass through without noticing it. The best part is that is FREE!!! There are three buildings in the yard- the resident bungalow, a clinic, and a "bachelor" house which are todays gallery with relics of the past. You will be accompanied by the staff who not only acts as guide but also to ensure the safety of the exhibits and visitors.

Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles – Bangkok  A beautifully curated museum inside the Grand Palace complex! 👗✨  The Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles showcases the elegance and craftsmanship of Thai textiles and royal fashion. You can see stunning displays of traditional fabrics, handwoven materials, and outfits worn by Queen Sirikit during official ceremonies and royal events.  The museum is air-conditioned, quiet, and very well organized — a great place to cool down and enjoy some culture after exploring the Grand Palace.  The staff are kind and helpful, and information panels are available in both Thai and English. || Inside the palace stands a beautifully preserved European-style building. I honestly didn’t expect it to be this elegant. The exhibition showcases the late Queen’s actual dresses, and even though I went in with no expectations, seeing them up close was truly impressive.  The gold silk gown was absolutely stunning ⭐️ the fabric shimmered under the light, and the intricate patterns were exquisite.  For the other pieces, I kept thinking, “This still looks so modern,” and sure enough, they were designed by Pierre Balmain. Seeing Balmain’s work here was such an unexpected and special moment.  It took me about 40 minutes to walk through, and though the exhibit is small, it’s beautifully curated and well worth a visit if you’re already exploring the palace grounds. 👑✨ || Wasn’t sure whether to visit this museum or not, but very happy I did.  The story behind Thai traditional clothing is truly unique, and you can learn about it in a fun way. There’s interactive screens, and a short history film on a loop (definitely watch it).  The exhibited pieces are stunning. If you’re into fashion and history, do not miss this one. Queen Sirikit’s story is really beautiful and unique.  The visit is included with your Grand Palace entrance ticket. || Beautiful museum. Located within the grounds of the royal palace. Ticket for the royal palace gains your entrance to the museum. Several rooms with lots of detail about how Queen Sirikit influenced Thai dress and culture. || I am a HUGE fan of all museums but this one was so special and glamorous. Absolutely loved seeing the Queens dresses and gowns. Don't skip it thinking it is not worth it It is definitely worth a visit. A lot of history behind the dresses. Unfortunately no pictures from inside. || Very nice place for a visit, not a big museum but has lots of historical information about Thai costume as well as the outfit that Queen Sirikit actually wore in the past || For foreigners, entry is already included in the Grand Palace ticket. However, Thai visitors need to pay an additional 150 THB. I only visited the shop area and didn’t go into the exhibition itself, but I absolutely loved the building — it’s beautifully designed.  The shop features a great selection of traditional textiles and patterns, including silk from different provinces across Thailand. Even as a Thai, I found it really educational — there were so many things I didn’t know before. It’s a great spot to learn and appreciate the richness of Thai craftsmanship and culture. || While those flocking to the popular tourist destination may only focus on the Emerald Buddha, architecture and looming demons, more demons – and monkeys and princes – can be found inside a two-story, Victorian-style building near the main entrance: the Queen Sirikit Museum of Textiles.  On the second floor find two exhibitions: Khon costumes and Queen Sirikit’s creations made by by French designer Pierre Balmain  The two rooms present the museum’s highlight: Costumes designed by renowned Parisienne couturier Balmain worn by the Queen during a six-month tour of the United States and Europe in 1960 with King Bhumibol, when she was toasted as the height of fashion  While looking at the clothing, see photographs of Her Majesty wearing the exhibited pieces along with high-quality footage of Their Majesties during their visits abroad from 1960 to 1973  The exhibitions launched Aug. 12 to celebrate the Queen’s 84th birthday and runs through June 2018.  Admission is 150 baht for adults, 80 baht for seniors over 65, and 50 baht for students and children. Children under 12 and visitors to the Grand Palace who purchase the palace tickets get in free. Visitors in wheelchairs are welcome.  The museum is open daily from 9am to 4:30pm. Last admission at 3:30pm || 3 galleries with absolute Thai culture and education on textile and really bringing out the pride in Thai wear and textiles. It was an eye opener to see decades of style and ageless beauty. Would take 30 mins to 1 hour to cover the 3 galleries, depending on how fast you go through the place. Loved the gift shop as well for different options, as well as the activity room to further showcase Thai culture and beliefs. || The highlight of our Grand Palace visit. An extensive collection of beautiful clothing displaying both traditional and modern fabrics. The information regarding the Royal Family and Court life is very interesting and helpful. Lovely gift shop. Helpful and welcoming staff. No photography allowed of the clothing on display. You need your Grand Palace ticket for entry.

place_name: Chulalongkorn University Museum of Natural History
reviews_content: When you like bones and Victorian  Curiousity Cabinet style museums, as I do, this one is great. It is not big, but full of display cases with interesting specimens. Texts are all in Thai, but it is after all a small and completely free museum provided by the university. The only downside for me was the very bad state of the taxidermy, but since this is not a climate controlled museum and only has standard display cases, I fear thar is down to the general climate in the city. Too bad, but changing that would be very expensive.  It is not wheelchair accessible as it is quite cramped and includes a set of stairs. || This museum is a part of science faculty building, which kinda explain why it's only open during weekdays and barely has any English text.  Other than that, this is probably the best natural science museum in Thailand with multiple specimens from both vertebrates and invertebrates animals in both forms of dry taxidermy, chemical taxidermy, skeleton/shells, and other animal parts. Excellent for studying as each specimen is a really well preserved form of animals that 80-90% of them are well taken care of regulary (some of them is visibly lack of care/really old that part of the skin is withering away further more or their preserved chemicals turn yellow).  This place also shows multiple scientists' achievements related to each room and other local technologies associated with. || An interesting place to visit to know more about Thailand's natural history. || It’s a very nice place for introverts. Despite the place that is not so large, the collection is pretty much. There’s no guide. Not so many people came when I visited there, I even was alone at first until someone came in after 30-45mins.  For foreign visitors, I recommend you to bring your smartphone to translate the information of collection because mostly it is written in Thai Language only.  Free entry. || We really liked it, thank you! It turned out to be a free museum by the university. However, at first I was confused that there were no people anywhere, no guards. But apparently it's free and it's normal. || My recent visit to the Chulalongkorn University Museum of Natural History left me with a profound sense of disappointment. Upon arriving at the museum, I was met with a locked door and a complete lack of any signage indicating closure. This resulted in a wasted trip and a significant inconvenience.  The museum's failure to provide clear and visible information regarding its closure is unacceptable. Visitors should not be left guessing about the museum's operating hours, especially when traveling to a specific location with the intention of visiting.  While I could glimpse some of the exhibits from outside the museum, this was far from a satisfactory experience. The true value of a museum lies in the ability to interact with the exhibits and gain insights from knowledgeable guides. Without access to the interior, I was deprived of the museum's intended purpose.  The lack of transparency regarding the museum's closure and the inability to fully experience the exhibits warrant a single-star rating. I urge the museum's management to take immediate steps to improve communication with visitors and ensure that the museum is accessible during its advertised operating hours.  **Recommendations:**  * Implement clear and visible signage indicating closure dates and times. * Provide advance notice of closures on the museum's website and social media platforms. * Consider offering online virtual tours or exhibits during periods of closure.  By addressing these shortcomings, the Chulalongkorn University Museum of Natural History can regain the trust of visitors and establish itself as a reliable and worthwhile destination. || The museum is very small and there are no conditioners, only fans, so it is hard to stay there for more than 30 minutes. But I give it 4 stars because it's free and at least there is one museum like this one in Bangkok. But I would like it to be bigger and with better air conditioning system. || Great free, self service museum. It's a bit dimly lit and a bit overcrowded.. But it is free and has lots of wet and dry specimens.  If you're interested in the Thai local natural history, or you like science and are in the area, try to visit all the free university museums, there are quite a few on the campus. Take note that many of them only open on certain days and for short hours, so do plan your trip well in advance and watch the time! || Was a bit disappointed that the big room is under renovation. However, the department students & staffs here are helpful & friendly make it up for us. Other rooms are available upon request. We visited turtle room, insect room & snail room. Probably it’s best to come after renovation work is done. || Very authentic old style museum, it's wooden floors that you have to walk barefoot. Very nice exposition, highly recommend for visiting.

Extremely impressive complex of several specialized museums, including four (general medicine, pathology, forensic, parasitology) in that very same location. Very informative, bilingual, however, I don't think general visitors should find its display interesting and appealing, as some parts of it may look pretty shocking to those far from medicine, forensic or crime investigation.  Photography is strictly prohibited inside museums. My photos shown here were made from museum entrances. || A little hard to review this place. It’s very informative but you need a strong stomach to go here. There is actually 3 museum and they cost 100 baht each. Free for Thai. All three museums have some interesting stuff but lots of dead bodies and babies in jars. So if you don’t mind seeing that this place is for you. It also has a bit of a hospital smell. I’ve added some pictures of the exhibit that are appropriate but not of the dead bodies inside, just be warned! Some pictures are of the other two museums, my favorite was the boat museum which has the largest wooden boat ever found underground and also no dead bodies at the boat museum || If you have a lot of time in Bangkok and you like museums, the make sure to visit this museum. You can buy 1 ticket that covers 3 buildings. Even though I am not that much interested in the medical stuff, I still found this place interesting and worth it. || Fantastic Museum of Anatomy, Pathology,  Parasites, Medical Museum.  This museum let's you get a real life up close view of real bodies and all parts inside of bodies, great selection variety of specimens, curated in a very respectful way in a medical facility.  Definitely worth a visit, to see, up close how we all are made.  Amazing 💛 || Nice place to visit for doable price if you're interested in anatomy and the hunan body. I do think it's quite a shame that for the medical museum part most description are only in Thai. || A definite stop for those that have any interest in this amazing place. I thoroughly enjoyed my time from start to finish. Top notch educational experience for anyone interested in medicine, anatomy, forensics, or just the macabre  The exhibits are deeply informative, a bit intense, and seriously one-of-a-kind. It’s not your average museum and that’s the point. You’re getting honest displays of the human body and medical history. If you have a weak stomach, find someplace else for your sensitive nature.  As for the 1-star reviews? Ignore them. They’re clearly from people who either didn’t understand the complex or probably shouldn’t have visited a museum like this in the first place.  Only thing of note that can be taken negatively is the lack of AC, but they have open windows and fans blowing, so if you can handle that, this is an amazing stop to add to your itinerary! Take my advice, don’t miss this if you’re nearby and have the time to do it! || My friend had a medical appointment at the hospital, so I decided to visit the museum while waiting for him. Paid 200 Baht which gave me access to all three (maybe it’s a special thing during COVID-19), and I spent two hours visiting everything. I enjoyed all the display of anatomical, forensic, cultural, and historical perspectives. || Siriraj Medical Museum is definitely one of the top museum in Thailand. If not, one of the best in South East Asia. Whether you are here for academic research or just to wonder around to kill off some time.  The easiest way to reach here is via ferry (siriraj pier), opposite to tha prachan pier.  As many google reviewer says, although it is quite an adventure but surely is not for the faint of heart. Please do eat before you visit the space, and definitely not for children under 15 yrs old.  There are 3 museums split inside. Dont worry, the counter receptionist will guide you with a leaflet (Eng Language as well) and there are English signage from one museum to another as well.  Photos are not allowed except for the Siriraj Bimuksthan Museum and the pre historic building where you can get to know more during the area within WWII.  Medical students, there should cover you many aspects of medical care, theory and researches purpose. But for quite - squeamish person like myself, I still do enjoy it, but it is very disturbing when seeing corpses and trauma injuries (homicide, suicide etc) graphic visuals.  There is some audio tech to assist you for Non-Thai speakers. Not too sure about "request touring" for Eng language. Would be great to have one at an additional cost. When I was there, I only witnessed Thai Speaking small group tour/walk through.  Ticket Prices for Local: 80 THB Ticket Prices for Foreigners: 250 THB  This is an international level museum. Truly remarkable. Worth the visit. Highly Recommend.  Do check their facebook page a day before you pay a visit. Incase they, closed for covid19 pandemic etc. || This museum is not for the faint of heart, many graphic images of victims, live specimens as well as crime evidence.  200baht per person if you're a tourist. Can be purchased at the museum itself.  There are 2 buildings for the medical/pathology museum. There's also a history museum nearby for an additional 100baht.  Very interesting and educational experience overall.  All the explanations were mostly in Thai language as well as some in English.  (No photos allowed inside) || Quite the experience seeing all the bodies with your own eyes rather than virtually through pictures or youtube. Would’ve given 5 stars if there were more English labels. 300baht for each museum (medical/historical).  Definitely a place to visit when in Bangkok.

Great place to explore architecture from the beginning of XX century, the time of HM Rama VI. It is the Thai palace constructed with the references to the different European styles. There is even the Hall in Bysantian style. On some marble blocks of the floor ancient sea creatures fossiles can be seen. The visit is possible in the morning or from 1:30 pm. Better to contact them in advance for the English speaking guide.  There is a nice cafe in the entrance of the palace, sharing the Place's interior and style. Even menu looks like the artefact from the past. Worth to be visited.  The cafe has good coffee ☕ || A must visit place. Sit besides the Ratchawitee road, near Victory monument. Should call for the tour guide if you want to know the history in depth. Dress properly. || Only open to the public on Saturday and Sunday 2 slots a day 9:30~11:30 and 13:30~15:30. You can come earlier to buy the ticket before the tour begins. Each tour takes about 2 hours to complete. There's a restaurant in the palace. || One of the European style palaces That are still open to the public but only on Saturday and Sundays. Very interesting architecture and history. You have to join a Thai language tour which is included in the entrance price (60 baht up to pension age and 30 baht for oldies) but you can break away shortly after the start 😃. … || Beautiful building and place. There are guided tours here. But you can come during the castle's opening hours and walk around independently the house and grounds. It's a very beautiful and unusual place for Asia. || What an amazing experience visiting the palace, frist of all the provided tour guide was super informative, polite and kind. The whole visit was based around her (the tour guide), she knew a lot about Thai history and the way she told the story was very captivating and fun to imagine along with her. The palace is still in a very good condition and filled with memories. I would recommend visiting here. Two thumbs up. || My friend (tourist) wanted to come here I didn’t know such a place existed! The palace was closed (only open for weekends) yet the cafe open everyday.  If you are around area it’s nice to stop by. Parking are free.  No Credit card || One of the most beautiful historical places. It was a palace but now turned to be a museum. The entrance fee is reasonable and the cafe is wonderful. U can come and take a photo as well as have a great meal here. No parking place, but it's easy to access by public transportation. || "Beautiful and Romantic Palace" There are 2-3 rounds (9:30, 13:30 and maybe possibly additional round) of guided walk-around. Recommend to attend it as you can go to other floors which are not generally opened to all. The guides are trained graduates from Royal school and they are very keen in speaking English. Fee is very affordable at THB 60 for anyone regardless of Thai or foreigner. Please come on time for the guided visit. The tour takes around 1-1.5 hr. After finishing the visit, you may take a rest at the cafe on the first floor. || Got a chance visiting in Night museum period. Ticket for 100 baht, you got a tour guide describe a history of the palace. A little bit boring in some point but overall was a fantastic night.

Unless you're on a tour you can only walk the corridors and gardens. You can't go inside any rooms or upstairs. For THB30 recommend a tour available on weekends at 9:30 and 10:30 am. But better to check the times for any updates. || I once considered holding our wedding celebration in this beautiful throne hall that captivated me with its blend of Thai and colonial design, green pastel color, and decor. Unfortunately, the venue turned out to be too small for our gathering. I still have a deep affection for this place. || The building is beautifully decorated.It's a part of Phayathai Palace. || Beautiful throne room! || It's a must, if you love arts. Inside, there are wonderful paint on the ceiling. || This place is amazing I M speechless

place_name: ซุ้มประตูเฉลิมพระเกียรติ 6 รอบพระชนมพรรษา
reviews_content: You know you’re in Chinatown the moment you see it - big, bold, and iconic. It’s a great landmark and photo spot that really sets the vibe. However it’s quite hard to cross the street there. The traffic is hectic and there’s no clear crosswalk. Still, a cool spot that kicks off the Chinatown experience. || A traditional Chinese gate that marks the entrance to Chinatown. Beautiful, but not something to stop for. You take two or three pictures and continue on your way. || When we make a trip to Chinatown we take the subway and walk on down to Chinatown Gate. It's a great way to start a visit to Chinatown and great place for pictorial. From there we continue to walk on down into Chinatown. Highly recommended stop. || An easy 7 minute walk from the Hua Lamphong MRT station, the route takes you past the impressive main Bangkok Train depot, and this landmark visit is well worth your time. || "Commonly known as the Thai-Chinese Cultural Archway, it is located at the site of the former fountain roundabout or 'Odeon Circle'.  Located on Tri Mit Road, Talat Noi Subdistrict, Samphanthawong District, Bangkok, before entering Yaowarat Road.  This archway is built in Chinese architectural style, with most materials imported directly from China.  It was constructed by the Thai-Chinese community and various government agencies as a royal merit offering on the occasion of His Majesty King Bhumibol Adulyadej's 6th cycle birthday anniversary in 1999." || I’ve been to many places called China town around the world. Never seen anything dirty like this. Lots of crowds though . Food all over streets looks very unclean , I was afraid to touch any. Maybe I’m too sensitive. Just my humble opinion. Looks not hygienic! And some smell - some places was terrible . || To avoid the weekend crowd, go during the weekdays. You'll never go hungry in Chinatown and there's so many stalls with different offerings. This place is a must-see and visit when you're in Bangkok. || One of the historical sites in China Town, Yaowarat Road. It's located near the old temple of the Golden Buddha statue. Very beautiful, free to visit. Walking along the road to other attractive sites is very nice. || Entrance to Chinatown In the streets parallel to Chinatown, you can find a variety of delicious food. || A little tricky to cross to but it is a roundabout. Great view of the Wat from the north side of the square.  Drop by before 5pm to avoid the Chinatown madness and traffic.

It's a small palace from King Rama 6. Some part has been converted to be part of the hospital.  The guided tours are only available on Saturday and Sunday, at 9am and 1pm. Entrance fee is THB 40. || This small villa is just in the backyard of Phayathai Palace. It is worth a visit. || Nice ambiance :D with a small lovely house! || Part of the Phayathai Palace garden || I was able to visit during the time the guide gave me, gained historical knowledge and many stories about the personal past of King Rama VI. || It's worth taking a walk around the neighborhood. || Interesting location. The walk was worth it; it's a beautiful place. || The residence behind the palace is very beautiful, but it would be even more stunning with a little landscaping.

Well well it was good. I mean the you get the view of the whole city. Skywalk was meh! But the view is great. Sky-verse is okayish. Didn’t try the tilt but I think that will be worth it || We booked our visit to Mahanakhon SkyWalk in Bangkok on GetYourGuide and it was one of the most memorable parts of our trip today 🌆. From the moment we arrived at the King Power Mahanakhon building the experience felt special and well organised. The lobby and digital displays set the scene, and the elevator ride up was fun and fast. Once we reached the observation levels we were blown away by the panoramic views of the Bangkok skyline 🌇 and city life below 📸.  ￼  Being able to walk out onto the glass floor at 314 meters above the streets was unforgettable and gave a thrilling sense of height and perspective. The indoor 360 degree observation deck on the 74th floor was stunning with views in every direction and perfect lighting for photos. The outdoor decks on the 78th floor let us take in even wider views of Bangkok, and it truly felt like we were on top of the world 🗺️.  ￼  The staff were helpful and friendly throughout our visit which made everything feel smooth and welcoming. We spent a relaxed few hours taking photos, soaking in the skyline, and just enjoying the unique vantage point of the city. The whole experience was worth doing and something I would recommend to anyone visiting Bangkok, especially if you love views and photography ❤️.  If you are organising your visit on GetYourGuide you can use discoun code TRAVELWIZZARD5 for a better price 💰. It adds a nice little saving and makes this incredible experience even more accessible. || Nice experience and Bangkok view at High altitude building yey || Crazy view, especially during sunset. But overly priced for the experience, ultimately it’s only a view and glass walk. Mostly very crowded at that. || Did the skywalk/sky glass at sunset. Amazing experience. Highly recommended. || Love the thrill and experience when you reach the top. There’s no other place that we have been to that the top is open space. || Good experience, touristy overpriced food so avoid eating there. Sunset is the best time to visit and tickets are cheaper online and also avoid long queues. Booking on trip was the cheapest. No time limit once up there. SkyVerse is overrated but the ticket is generally sold as combo || Amazing wonderful too good super kya view hai from top and glass....walk on 78 flr is the Amazing wonderful....too scary but outstanding too good feeling....muat must do when u r un bang kok....  Tilt is another different level think u must do....plus sky verse is also...roo fun too good...  Please guys go have fun || MahaNakhon was fantastic fun and a highly recommended experience. The staff were super friendly throughout our experiences (Skywalk, Skyverse and the VR). We arrived mid morning and I would suggest arriving early as we noticed it got significantly busier around lunch, and other punters were a little pushy trying to get their perfect Instagram shots (which is just not our style). It was also quite hot on top of the building so a hat and sunscreen is highly recommended. Also it is very high and the glass skywalk should definitely make you a little shaky in the knees, but awesome and definitely worth the trip. The other bonus is, once you are in you can technically take as little or as long as you like, even when we took our time and had a lunch break in the food court nearby, it was about 3hrs. Very easy to get to on the Silom BTS line and is literally signposted when you get off at Chong Nonsi station. || Was soo fantastic times! 😍❤️🙏 …

Fort Inthasangsan is one of the many forts surrounding the Grand Palace. It's located on the corner between Tha Chang and Silpakorn University. Below this fort is a newly constructed tunnel, now open, that leads from Tha Chang to the Grand Palace. || It is believed to have been built during the reign of King Rama II and demolished during the reign of King Rama V to improve Maharat Road. Currently, a tunnel has been built across the road, allowing us to see some of the remains of the fort and the remaining walls, including cannons and wheels found in the area of ​​the fort. || If you get off at Chang to visit the Grand Palace or Wat Pho on the Chao Phraya Express, you'll find yourself in the area where the boats exit Talat. The tuk tuks staying in this area are used to tourists in a bad way, so be careful. It's also nice to take a leisurely stroll to Wat Pho. || From what I understand, a fortress is used here to refer to any point where guard posts or military structures were erected along the perimeter walls of the splendid Royal Palace. This one, like the others I saw in the area, is characterized by a splendid white color and incredibly well-maintained, enhancing its beauty despite its simple structure. || One of the many forts surrounding the Grand Palace, located at the corner before boarding the ferry. || Unique and convenient

place_name: บ้านแม่นาย

reviews_content: Typically, this would be 4 stars as it's a nice little pedestrian bridge, but while I was there I stopped and looked around, and it was just so beautiful.  The canal and the landscaping are extremely attractive as are the viewable parts of the nearby temples.  And as I stood there I was amazed at just how wonderful this little bridge was and the city surrounding it. || THIS WALKWAY BRIDGE WAS BUILT BY SOMDET PHRASRI PHATCHARINTHRA PHRABOROMMARACHININAT, THE QUEEN OF KING RAMA V IN 1911. SHE GRANTED THE CONSTRUCTION COST TO COMMEMORATE HER FOURTH CYCLE (48 YEARS OLD) BIRTHDAY, WHICH FELL ON THE YEAR OF PIG. AT THE BEGINNING, THE BRIDGE HAD NO GIVEN NAME UNTIL A PIG MEMORIAL WAS BUILT NEARBY, SO IT WAS CALLED SAPHAN MU (PIG BRIDGE) OR SAPHAN PI KUN (YEAR OF PIG BRIDGE). THE BRIDGE HAS FOUR DECORATIVE POSTS SYMBOLIZING BIRTHDAY CANDLES OF FOURTH CYCLE, AND THE OVAL PLATES ON EACH POST MEANS THE CYCLE OF BIRTHDAY. || Preserved historic bridge. || small old pedestrian bridge over tne khlong || One of historical landmarks in Bangkok. || Pikun Bridge in front of Wat Ratchaprathit...crosses the old city moat. The bridge over the canal is not very large but is strikingly beautiful with its Western art, white and green, near the Pig Monument. || Pikun Bridge This bridge crosses the old moat in front of Wat Ratchabophit, near the Pig Monument. It serves as a crossing point between Wat Ratchaprathit and Wat Ratchabophit Sathit Maha Simaram. The bridge itself is a simple white structure with a European style. || The bridge over the old city moat is not small, not big, but it is strikingly beautiful. It is white and green, near the Pig Monument. Look carefully because it is not very big and has a pavilion to protect it. It is better to come early in the morning because there is not much shade in that area.

A good pier that is in walking distance to many major attractions. It has shops close to the entrance which are convenient whilst waiting for a boat and interesting to browse. reviews_content: The hotel is very big and we were part of a large group. The hotel is old school, with big wooden keychains with keys to the rooms, lots of wood everywhere. Additionally, the luggage storage service was convenient and efficient, making our departure stress-free.  Another great feature of this hotel is its location. The surrounding area has a great selection of Indian food options, which made us feel right at home.  I have already recommended this hotel to all my friends traveling with family and kids, and I would highly recommend it to anyone visiting Bangkok. Thank you, Bangkok Palace Hotel, for making our stay so memorable! || The Hotel offers a convenient location near Pratunam, making it easy to access shopping areas and public transport. The lobby and common areas are spacious, and the staff are generally polite and helpful. However, some rooms feel a bit old … || We stayed at Bangkok Palace hotel for one night and that I was happy that it was that 1 night only. Location: The hotel location is really pathetic with slum area around it.  Rooms: Hotel itself while being huge, it’s quite old and rooms are in dilapidated state. Cupboards were dusty and entire room in dire need of renovation.  Checkin and Checkout process: Even the checkin and checkout process are both made in such an unfriendly way that its a mood spoiler from the beginning. They take security deposit of 1000THB in cash despite writing that credit card is acceptable. And there is whole process during checkout to get that back which takes atleast 10 mins or more.  Staff: The receptionist also quite rude during the entire interaction. No one was there to guide in parking our car which led to further confusion while unloading luggage. Seeing our luggage, staff sighed so heavily as if we have so many bags ( we had 4-5 bags for 3 people). After keeping luggage, the person kept standing expecting tip which I would have given had they not been too rude about the luggage. The only person who smiled during our stay was the person who calls the lifts. Everyone else had attitude!  Overall: The entire experience was pathetic and disappointing given the size of the hotel. Definitely NOT recommended!

Local small food court for mostly locals working in the area. Had the pork offal dark soup. Very tasty and affordable. Vendor speaks a bit of English so its great for my orders with extra tofu and no noodles. Cost me 90 baht. Delicious || I love this place. It's mostly Thai people grabbing breakfast on the way to work. There are several stalls with different choices. The menus are in Thai, but the vendors speak enough English to get by, and you can always use Google translate.  The food is outstanding. Everyone is very friendly. If you enjoy a more local experience I think you'll like it. There are fans so there are minimal bugs however there is no AC so can be a little hot and humid inside. Still worth the visit. || This place open its shutters at 4am for food prep and start serving only after 5 ish. There are 6 individual stalls, one selling drinks. By 2pm the stall selling different main & side courses to go with rice have not much left. We had the Kway Chap which is the Pork meat & offals with rice noodles, really tasty. But if business is good that day, there isn’t much left so no point going after 2pm. Food is as local as you can get, tasty and cheap. || Really delicious, affordable, authentic local food! very local and authentic thai food. there is a satay stall in front (so goood! i order it everytime) and the price is very reasonable || I got a tom yum soup. Prices are reasonable. I had Som Tum and Mango sticky rice the first night and Phanaeng chicken the next.  I came tonight again for the Som Tum.   Yummmmm.   I like that dish and this is one of the best I had!  All the food here is affordable and delicious.  Highly recommended for local food with out the Farang surcharge….  😁 || Ordered food from the right side furthest stall from the entrance  The dishes: Stir Fried Pork Belly with Kale Pork Neck Salad Tofu omelette Stir Fried Pork Basil with Egg Grilled pork neck  All of them were yummy, but the grilled pork neck & pork neck salad were my favorite 👌  For dessert, Sticky mango rice from the stall at the entrance. The lady was a pro, she peeled & cut mango super fast 👏 It was superb. Sweet mango, savoury sticky rice & coconut sauce were a perfect combination.  I've been to this food court 3x already. But i will definitely visit it again on the next Bangkok trip || Glad to discovered this kind-of hidden Thai food gems, which is close to BTS Station. The food was good too. || Nice basil pork rice. reviews_content: Excellent service and Amazing food.  Cost is on the higher side but the for Indians craving authentic Indian taste, it's worth it. The atmosphere is casual and colorful — just like a real Indian street stall — and the staff is friendly and quick. If you’re craving fun, flavorful, no-nonsense Indian comfort food, Chowpati is absolutely worth a visit. 🌶️🍛✨ || After days of Thai street food, I was craving Indian flavors — and Chowpati didn’t disappoint! reviews_content: My experience was truly elevated by my masseuse, P'Jane. Her skill is exceptional; she has ability to locate and release tension exactly where it lives, hitting every targeted muscles and joints.It was less of a generic rub and more of a personalized treatment.  ***Foot reflexology needs improvement--to put more pressure on. But the Deep tissue massage treatment is spot on. Felt relaxed and released.  The staff throughout the spa are wonderfully attentive and create a calm, welcoming atmosphere.  *** Tucked conveniently next to a charming art and craft studio cafè, (TaiBan) it’s an ideal setup for a friends' day out—you can enjoy a creative session and then unwind completely, all in one trip. 👍 || I had the Deep Tissue Massage and thought it would be very painful, but it wasn’t. It was the best massage I’ve ever had, it really hit the sore spots in my muscles. The place feels very serene and relaxing, with a touch of greenery from the plants. Truly relaxing and reasonably priced. You have to book a slot in advance since they usually get fully booked throughout the day, but luckily, I was able to get a last-minute slot. || Came here this evening for essential oil massage and was really impressed!
