Thanks for visiting - we hope to see you at the Box sometime soon 😏 … || cool place to see local musicians! went to a hip hop evening had a great time. there's a hotdog shop inside and two bar counters, and it's straight up nice to be there. check their website for upcoming events || Like all great venues before them, With its longevity, consistency and authentic diy music culture, Speaker box remind predominant in the local music scene.  The venue recently renovated and moved to a bigger space with bar area and clean toilet, walking distance from the OG spot.  The live room capacity is about 200 - 250 max. Decent size for an intimate live music experience. Do check out their calendar before hand as they only have bands for event nights only. On the other hand, the bar area is always open most nights. Drinks start at around 100+ baht. If you’re looking for a music venue in Bangkok, this is definitely one of the place worth checking out. || Thanks for visiting and supporting the Independent Live Music scene in Bangkok! We hope to see you again soon! || Amazing venue, great band curation… I just wish the stage was a little higher so folks at the back could see the great musicianship from the bands playing 💚 … || Thanks for visiting! We hope to see you again soon! || Had my doubts until I saw the performances on the back stage area. The beer wasn't overpriced either, pricey but not ridiculous! || Thanks for visiting! We hope to see you again soon!  We also have a happy hour from 17:30 to 20:30 😏 … || It's a good place for live indy music in English language. There are 2 rooms there both with bars. So if you don't enjoy the live music, the other room is a place to hang out with friends. || Nice venue, has a dancefloor, smoking area as well as a chill area where you can play pool. Staff is also very friendly! || Thanks for visiting! We hope to see you again soon! || With the latest venue’s light and sound production and stage setting, Speakerbox has become one of the best live house & bar with the mix of cool underground electronic music zone, a place that will satisfy true music lovers, both old-school and experimental alike. || Thanks for visiting and supporting the Independent Live Music scene in Bangkok! We hope to see you again soon!

Went here during WIM concert. The hall was really functional, cool AC and lightning and can accommodate few thousands of people || came here and got a table for New Year’s and it was completely empty. service also took forever even though there was no one in the club. they wouldn’t give us a refund either but we didn’t even get any drinks !!! stay away. || My daughter did a show || A food court to get lost in

Fantastic! Watched BrokeBoysClub live and couldn't be any happier. Fantastic sound and a very intimate setting. The staff were super friendly too. || The sound was great! The band selection was immaculate. It’s nice to discover new local bands who are really skilled and passionate with what they are producing || I recommend the best livehouse . The atmosphere here is very good.  The lighting, colors, and sound are all superb. the staff are also lovely. There are also artists merchandise for sale in front. The artists who came performed very well. The people at the event were lovely. Easy to get to., there is a Chinese temple in front. || Possibly one of the best music venue in Bangkok right now, like all great grassroots venues, the place is self operated by passionate group of music lovers, definitely a good place to start if you wanna meet the locals and as well as international depending on the events, do check their calendar before hand, as they only open on concerts night || The best livehouse in town, with a great sound system and reasonably priced drinks and tickets. || Came here looking for rock music in Bangkok and was actually quite pleasantly surprised. This room is not big, but it is big enough to present wonderful music live . The staff at this livehouse are very friendly and the atmosphere is good. But I am confused that last night's show also checked my passport, even though it claimed there was no age limit. || The age check was to determine whether the audience is over the drinking age or not (in Thailand it is 20 years old). If you are under the drinking age, you are welcome as well but you will get different wristband color that will prohibit you to buy alcohol beverages.  We are also strict about buying alcohol for underage drinkers as well, those who violate our rules will be forced to leave the premises and have their wristbands cut.  Thank you! || Cool small local venue, which has an intimate feel and great sound if you want to see your bands up close and personal. Drinks were also reasonably priced and it was easy to get to with a good selection of restaurants and other food options nearby. We saw Yellow Fang supported by Daniel Ryn, and are looking forward to seeing more Indie bands there in the future! You also get the free entertainment of watching people from the upstairs terrace bail while practising their surfing at Flow House downstairs. || very weird location for live music venue. its above a watersport venue, so watch music and see people struggling with indoor waves below. food and beverages are sold below but may ran out of beer if there's huge crowd. small and intimate venue. || Pretty cool venue. Basically just a box room with a stage at one end,  but sound was good, lighting OK and it's in an interesting location. Had a good night out here (saw Thai post rock band Hope the Flowers) and would certainly go back. You can walk here in about 15-20 mins from Phrom Pong || Easy access, one of the most friendly live house in BKK

place_name: หอแสดงดนตรี จุฬาลงกรณ์มหาวิทยาลัย (CU MUSIC HALL)
reviews_content: The hall is very nice, comfortable and is quite convenient to visit Also, it is suitable for various performing i.e., the concert, performance. || I am about to have a concert there || place for knowledge place for fun || It is a good work, joining together to spread the message of Buddhism, filling the four groups of Buddhists according to the teachings of the Lord Buddha. || I had the opportunity to see a play here for the first time. The play was fun and the Thai arts and culture were beautifully presented. Location: Clean, comfortable, with parking nearby. Follow the performances on CU Art Culture's Facebook page. || A solemn gathering of the nun sangha in this building. May the nun sangha continue to grow and progress in the Buddha Dharma. || I just went there for the first time and really liked it. The sound was good and the place wasn't too crowded. If I have the chance to go again, I will definitely go.

The venue is convenient with BTS access and locating in the prime location of sukhumvit. The venue is a great size where the audience can still enjoy the top shelf sound system (but still with 1 sec lagged on the LED screen) and the ability to see their favorite artist without the use of binocular. But thats where the positivities end. You better plan ahead since the traffic here by car is jammed pack 24/7. But the worst, the ABSOLUTE WORST, is the food. You'd think they'd take advantage of luring the paying audience who's basically stucked in the venue with at least human edible food.  But Noooooooo, they offer the overpriced, STALE, wilted, re-fried and yet managed to be icy cold finger foods. Want to go get something to eat downstairs in the 50+ restaurants available? Nah. They know the drill now. Now they REFUSED re-entry and they keep reminding us over the speaker every 10 secs. I wish there is a minus stars rating available and id have no quams giving this venue a minus 8. I am physically SICK eating their oil-drenched "chicken" and sausage wrapped in bacon. I'd need to go hurl in the toilet afterwards. Don't kid yourself when you see a lot of digits on your sales report. The only reason its high is becoz we are informed AT THE GATE after fighting the traffic and climbing 5 flights of stairs that no reentry is allowed. The notion of being stuck in the concert for 8 hours with no food and drinking on an empty stomach is the sole reason why we had to half-heartedly pay for it. Now im stucked in the venue with upset stomach instead. Total BS. Ps. On the bright side, they have massive washrooms with A/C so spending most of my time in here ain't so bad. Ps2. The management quick response is highly appreciated. Please at least provide more food selection as this has constantly been the issue everytime we come here for events. Looking forward to a positive change in the future. || Hi N N, Thank you for this detailed feedback. We are genuinely sorry that your experience, especially with the food, was so disappointing. The wellbeing of our guests is our top priority, and what you described is not the standard we aim for. While our F&B is managed by a partner, we are responsible for the quality. Your feedback has been shared with their senior team for review and action. We also understand your frustration with the no re-entry policy, which is set by the event organizer. We see how this, combined with your food experience, created a very poor experience. We will discuss this with the organizer for consideration with future events. Regarding traffic, being an exceptionally busy Halloween night. We always work to manage flow with the local police, but as you noted, the direct BTS connection is the most reliable and sustainable way to access the venue. We take your feedback seriously, as it's crucial for our improvement, and we sincerely hope this isn't the last time you visit us. We would appreciate the opportunity to welcome you back properly for a future event.  UOB LIVE || 7.00 PM: Arrived at Emsphere building for concert of Fred Again. 7.20 PM: After security check arrived at the event. 7.25 PM: Went into the queue for drinks. 9.00 PM: Finally got to the counter, nearly nothing left. Everything sold out and had to take what is left. 9.05 PM: Went inside to see Fred Again. 9.55 PM: End of show.  To summarize, security check + getting drinks took us 2 hours. We only got 55 minutes of our concert. Shame on you, UOB Live. You are robbers of our time. There were 3 drinks counters for 6000 people, what the heck? And don't even have enough drinks to cover for everyone.  Who planned this event at UOB Live? It is a true disgrace. Paid 4000 THB per person and we stood in the queue for 1.5 hours while the concert was ongoing!! Is this normal?  UOB should offer 50% refund to everyone due to this scandal, absolutely ridiculous. || We sincerely apologize for the wait you experienced. You came for the performance, not the pause and we’re sorry we let that get in the way. We’re working behind the curtain to make sure it doesn’t happen again. If you’d like to share more, we’re listening. || I go to concerts often, and this is my favorite hall, even though Sukhumvit Road is incredibly congested. Get there early and don't worry about parking fees, as UOB Live offers 12 hours of free parking! || Today I went to see Park Bogum at UOB live. It was my first time at the venue so I think I should write a review here for others.  Pros: New, clean, the process of picking up the ticket was smooth and fast, lots of restrooms on the 6th floor where the event was held overall experience was good with sound and screen (of course, nothing could go wrong with Park Bogum on the stage 🤣)  Cons: Can’t bring water, and when I bought water in front of the event venue, no bottle cap was provided, so I had to carry it anxiously trying so hard not to spill it on the floor (as a clumsy person it’s not really fun to have to do so 🙄🥺) turned out they didn’t allow that water we just bought inside the hall || Had a great time here, the sound was pretty well done (though it could be a bit quieter). The location is fantastic: very close to BTS and easily reachable by car. The security is very polite and they help in any way they can. They even had a first aid station which is awesome || Came here for the Sting concert and it's a great venue. Getting in was quick and easy, the toilets are huge so there was never any lines and when we arrived 45 minutes before the concert started there wasn't any lines for drinks either. Inside the sound was great and the floor seats were comfortable enough.  Our seats were on the floor in the middle at row 15, which was perfect. It's a fairly small venue so I don't think there are any really bad seat except for maybe the seats way out on either side.  One thing to mention is that I think they have made the stage a bit too low. If you are sitting on the floor and have a tall person in front of you they will block your view a bit unless you are also tall. Or if some inconsiderate people decide to stand up during the show they will basically block the view from everyone behind them. This happened a few times during the concert and people had to tell them to sit down. || We were excited to see Sean Paul. Got tickets to see him at the most expensive standing ticket which is the most up front.  Very disappointedly, the sound system is beyond anything i've ever experienced at a concert, probably the cheapest at the back is better. The low is so diluted we can barely feel and the mid and high are so low we can barely make out what's he is singing.  Had much higher standard for such location.  Wasted money and time to get through the traffic... totally would not recommend || Hi Kit P,   Thank you for taking the time to share this. We are genuinely sorry to hear that your experience at the Sean Paul concert fell short of expectations.   Hearing that the sound was unclear from your position is a concern for us. We want every guest to have an incredible experience.   While the final sound mix for any tour is at the discretion of the artist's and promoter's audio team, we work closely with them to ensure they can get the best performance from our venue. UOB LIVE is equipped with a world-class L-Acoustics K2 sound system, and our walls are fitted with acoustic panels specifically to prevent the kind of sound dilution you described.   Your feedback is invaluable in helping improve sound checks at future events. Best regards,   UOB LIVE || Excellent new venue in Empshere. Saw slot machine here and they were great. The sound was very good and the stage was a lot bigger than I expected. I am looking forward to seeing many more performances there. It is so nice to have a more accessible venue in the centre of Bangkok. || A huge thank you for the fantastic 5-star review! We're thrilled you enjoyed your experience with us :) || Went here for Valorant Masters. Awesome venue. Great people management. Really well built. Toilets really nice || Totally unprepared to host large artists and sold out events. Only three small bars open, with three people serving per bar, for over 6000 attendees - completely nonsensical. People had to queue for over an hour to get drinks (even non-alcohol ones) and subsequently missed the performances they had to paid to see. At one point the bars ran out of water, which is dangerous, and would have been preventable with some basic planning. Unsurprisingly, people passed out in the crowd.  The bar staff tried their best under difficult circumstances, but the organizers and management need to take responsibility and make some big improvements. || We're so sorry that your experience at UOB LIVE didn’t go as smoothly as it should have. We never want a night out to turn into a test of patience. We’re taking your feedback seriously and are working behind the scenes to make sure your next visit is a whole lot better.   Please share your thoughts with us at uoblive.asia@gmail.com.

Looking forward to seeing it. || Great project coming! || Good time lots of fun || Bangkok Arena, Bangkok's largest indoor multi-purpose arena, is set to open in 2028 alongside the Bangkok Mall, which is set to become the largest shopping mall in Southeast Asia. It will include a shopping mall, 15 cinemas, a water park, an amusement park, offices, condominiums, and a 51-story hotel, as well as a statue of the Goddess of Mercy. The Bangkok Arena is a world-class stadium with a capacity of 18,000, making it larger than the existing Impact Arena (which seats 12,000).

place_name: พิพิธภัณฑ์และหอจดหมายเหตุกรมประชาสัมพันธ์
reviews_content: Such an interesting place to visit. The staff there is very kind and friendly. They welcome me and my friend very warmly. Love the ancient vibe! || The staff are lovely, friendly, and very patient. There are so many songs to choose from. I really like it. I will definitely come back again when I have the chance.🤟🏻 || Exhibits the history of public relations in Thailand after the revolution and change of government until the present. You can see the old equipment of the Public Relations Department, including records, books, and various types of players. Before visiting, please contact the staff to make an appointment so that they can prepare for the tour and lecture. || The museum is located on the second floor of the auditorium building. There is an elevator and a ramp for wheelchairs and the elderly. Inside the museum is a collection of various items such as television cameras, photographic equipment, broadcasting equipment, and many sources of knowledge on communication. The Public Relations Department of Thailand has a history of the founders of public relations communication since its inception, providing a lot of knowledge. || Free admission. There are many old music vinyls, Thai songs, Luk Thung, Luk Krung, international songs, cartoon songs, movie soundtracks. The air conditioning is cool. The staff are very attentive. I recommend booking in advance. || Tuesday, July 16, 2024 - I had the opportunity to visit this museum and archive for the first time. It houses a large collection of records, including shellac records, totaling hundreds of thousands. Three donated record players are also available. Various broadcasting equipment is also included, all collected for study and learning. The staff were very welcoming and the tours were not tiring. Open daily, Monday through Friday, from 10:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Bangkok Design week 2025 || BANGKOK DESIGN WEEK 2023 The event runs until February 12th. The Post Office Building is located in the Pak Khlong Talat area. The exhibition features a projection mapping of flowers, which attendees have colored and scanned onto the building's walls. It's a truly beautiful display. I highly recommend coming to see it; you won't be disappointed. || I went during Bangkok Design Week 2024. The weather wasn't too hot yet, so it was convenient to travel. || Originally, this site belonged to the Department of Post and Telegraph and was the first post office in Thailand. Today, it houses a museum showcasing the history of Thai postal services.  I only recently discovered this museum thanks to Bangkok Design Week 2023. The building itself is beautiful.  However, its location makes it a bit difficult to access. I got lost driving around, crossing the river on several bridges.  I'll try to visit the interior when I have the chance and will provide a more detailed review later. || It's near the river, a nice place to relax, just a short walk away. || Bangkok Awakening 2025 Festival

This museum was an incredible experience. I loved the top floor that had the queen‘s actual outfits throughout the years, with information about the designers. But the first floor area with timeline information was incredible. Make sure you visit the first floor area and don’t just go up the stairs, you won’t regret it. The picture of the timeline I have is only the very first panel. || A very pleasant way to spend 1/2 day in Bangkok.  The grounds and buildings depict Thailand as it was in the 19th  and early 20th centuries - well before air conditioning.  Admission is restricted, call before visiting. || Always closed seems permanent from the policeman I asked || It’s closed for a while without knowing when it’s going to reopen. || Tried to visit today, but not possible to enter the site.

Absolutely LOVED it here! I can't believe that the museum is free to the public! Very few people were there when I went on a Saturday afternoon. The displays were informative, and did a wonderful job of telling a cohesive story about how money and institutions have been shaped by history. Definitely recommend checking it out if you have an interest in finance. || Absolutely wonderful experience in this hidden gem. Lots of interactive displays and the docents were really helpful in answering a range of questions. All exhibits are bilingually labelled and they go the extra mile to explain why the object is significant (eg, why early Thai banknotes are denoted in 6 languages, how rice production affects the monetary policy in Thailand, arbitraging the trade relations with China and Britain and why the constant struggle between different stabilisation/ pegging mechanisms, why bond was only issued almost four decades after BOT’s establishment, etc). Truly fascinating. The library features an outstanding collection of finance books over two floors. Where else in Bangkok can you find a full shelf of inflation-linked securities and MBS books in English for free? The museum also caters to visually-impaired visitors with touchable exhibits. Outstanding museum all around || The museum is located inside the Learning Center of the Bank of Thailand. Museum has 12:00-13:00 lunch brake.  NO NEED TO PAY MONEY 🤓 Children are welcome and friendly for people with disabilities too. There are brail signs around. Nice bathrooms as well.  Photograph and VDO friendly, visitors are allowed to spend time to record all objects inside, however, No touch at all and no food or drinks to inside museum.  There are four stories of displays with Thai officers accommodating with visitors, explanation can be in Thai or English.  Once the museum tour is at the end, visitors will come to the A Cup Cafe, so you can grab refreshment and bakery on your own expense. Price is affordable. || Admission is free. Tight security. They will scan your belongings. After the check, register yourself at the museum counter. The guide will bring you to the tour. The tour starts at the bottom of the room, which is 6 meter below the ground. Starting with coins, notes, and  details of the bank. Coins money has many history during those eras and in different sizes, coins from other countries such as Afgan, China, etc. Thailand officially print the notes themselves in year 1969. Back in 1902, it was printed in UK. 1941, due to invasion by Japanese, they had blocked UK from shipping the notes, therefore they had assigned Japan to print the notes.  After the world war, they requested US to print the notes and back to UK again in 1962. This building is next the river and you can enjoy the scenery before exit. || Went here when it was quiet, got warmly welcomed by the well spoken staff. Absolutely fantastic tour, way more in depth than I expected! Lots of history and well preserved building in amazing location. Definitely recommended for people interested in economics and numismatics. || Well-decorated free-entry library with great facilities. Can be here to get there. Good place for reading books or get some work done. Plenty of space tp settle, just look for the corner you prefer. I recommend this place personally if you’d love to spend a long time reading while resting your eyes with great Chaopraya riverside view with beautiful Rama8 bridge. || You can see the history of money in Thailand and enjoy the river views around the hangover bridge. Various notes and printing machines and alternative exchange materials. After touring, you can drink chill and nice drink in the coffee shop. || Nice building with a modern museum and Library. Coming at sunset is recommended, as the terrace affords lovely views of the river. I came during the Bangkok Art Biennial and there were some special exhibitions as well as the standard displays. || Really nice place. Museum was possible the best in Thailand, good information, interestingly presented, great English, interactive, related to wider history. For such a potentially boring topic it was a revelation. Also free parking, beautiful views. Even if you have no interest in the topic, worth a visit || Nice space for visiting and learning. The building is well designed. Inside is library, co-working space and museum. Outside is a view from Chaopraya river and Rama 8 bridge.

I wouldn't make this a priority visit but if you are passing, you could drop by. No admission fee, in fact  nobody else there apart from a couple of cleaners. Three House are configured around a square, all elavated above the ground on stilts. On the fourth side of the square, a small bridge leads over to a pavilion position above a pond. Two of the houses were locked when I visited, but the third was open and contained a  Buddha shrine together with a collection of musical instruments. || Not much to see here. Would not make a special trip. You can only look at the outside of the buildings. Photos on the university website give you an idea of what is here. || Restful.. But currently the walkways in the garden are under repair. Restful and calm space. No entrance fees. Not a must see venue. But worth it to get away from the hustle and bustle. || The Grandeur authentic traditional Thai architecture in the heart of Bangkok. Take every good care by the best University in South East Asia || Lovely old house on the grounds of the university || Beautiful. Well maintained || The weather is good, the water in the pond is very clean, there are very big fish, students like to feed them (bread). || The atmosphere is good and there is music to listen to. || Right in the middle of the university campus. Nothing special.

I’ve been traveling for 6 months around Southeast Asia and this was actually one of my favorite art galleries I’ve visited. The art is so vibrant and captivating. The museum was not crowded at all and super affordable (50 baht). There’s three floors and I might have gone back a second time to look at the art again if I had more time in Bangkok. Would definitely recommend if you are an art lover or looking for hidden gems in the city. || Based on reviews and the visit, the quality depends on what’s on. I got to see selected paintings from the local competition: some explores interesting concepts and social reality, some are mouthpieces. All skilfully drawn. All in all, depends on your interpretation of what is art and the current exhibit, it can be a meh to exceptional experience  50baht, cash/online transfer with QR code only || Popped in here randomly whilst killing time before my check-out. Well worth a visit if you're nearby and need a break from the heat. Great air-conditioning. 50 baht entry. I'm not that into galleries, but I really enjoyed this. Amazing art work across a few floors. Went on a monday lunchtime and there were maybe only 5 other people in there. || A small gallery with a rotating selection of mostly contemporary Thai art. Cheap admission, clean bathrooms, kind staff, and good AC. Not crowded at all. Definitely worth a visit especially on a hot day. || Great experience, welcoming staff and beautiful exhibits. Tales of history expressed on the first floor. We'll worth it experience, do check it out if you enter Thailand || One of the very attractive sites for art exhibition lovers. Entrance fee 50 Bth. All staff are very friendly and warmly welcoming as well as helpful. No other tourist people in the gallery, while we enjoyed spending our time together. So impressive! || A small gallery in the city center, where now, in September 2024, an exhibition of religious works is taking place. There are many very original paintings, it is worth visiting. But on the second floor it is unbearably hot (although the other floors have air conditioning), much hotter than outside, you will have difficulty looking at the paintings because you feel unwell. || If you look at previous posts here, you can see that there are some interesting exhibitions. But when I went there, the shown exhibition lacked artistic demands as well as curatorial standards.  In my opinion, the "art" on display had a purely decorative function and hardly any deeper meaning. The theme was transience, but it was treated in a superficial and clichéd manner.  In the entire three-story exhibition there were maybe 5 works that were somewhat interesting. A lot of it was really horrible kitsch. However, the purpose of the institution seems to be primarily to sell the works and not primarily to provide cultural education. I hope other exhibitions on site are more sophisticated. || A small but interesting art gallery. I explored it pretty much on my own. A nice place to see a different side of Bangkok. || It’s great art gallery in Bangkok old town. Nice decoration with valuable pieces. Ticket price quite affordable. Piece of art are temporary it’s will change every 2 month. I recommend to come by public transportation better. Due to parking lot quite a few.

Great art exhibitions, along with displays on the history of Chulalongkorn University. There are also some coloring activities available. Admission is free. || A museum with huge potential. Sadly my expectations were crushed as all the information is written in Thai. If you are an English only person like me make sure you have google translate on your phone and your phone fully charged. || This musuem showcasing the university progress and development as well as world leaders who visiting Chula U previously || I visited the Chulalongkorn University Museum for the Butterflies & Cockroaches exhibit, which, while enjoyable, fell short of my expectations. I anticipated a more expansive or detailed presentation. On the other hand, the permanent exhibit, which showcases the foundational history and legacy of Chulalongkorn University, exceeded my admittedly modest expectations. Unfortunately, some sections of the main exhibit were closed for maintenance during my visit, which was slightly disappointing. Overall, the temporary exhibit was intriguing but could have offered more, while the permanent exhibit effectively highlighted the university's rich history, despite some areas being inaccessible. || One of the most amazingly well-thought-out place for a museum. It has a lot of exhibition areas, and the Centenary exhibition truly open up my eyes for the partial history of the university itself. || Good place to know about the university || Great place, great exhibition but hardly find the parking lot || Best university of Thailand with superb atmosphere with nature and wonderful architecture of auditorium .

Modern clean facility with several theaters, including an Imax. Seats are soft, comfortable, and recline, sound system is clear and loud, but not run at ear-piercing levels. Theater temperatures are kept at a normal level, not too hot or cold, so no jacket needed.  Entrance to 4th floor cinema is much easier going through building B on the left side as you enter Quartier from the street or BTS level. || Cinema located at the top floor of Emquartier mall. It is accessible by escalator or elevator. Excellent service. This location has a lounge. Clean and impeccable.  We entered into the laser hall which was very trippy. Very nice theatre and very clean area. Really wish the movie theatres are super clean in America. || This cinema has become one of my go-to spots for watching IMAX mainly because I don’t have to deal with the traffic and crowds in central Bangkok like at Siam Paragon.  The IMAX theater here is new, clean, and well-maintained. The staff are always friendly and provide great service every time I visit.  To be honest, I actually find the overall system and experience here even smoother than at Paragon. It's also way less crowded, which makes the whole experience much more enjoyable.  During major movie releases, they often decorate the Box Office zone nicely or give out small goodies, which is a fun touch.  While some large-scale events or promotions may not be as big as what Paragon offers, this place is improving steadily and it’s definitely worth supporting. || The Management should regularly audit and anonymously review the service!  Staff on their phones while on duty (not just one but two of them)! Also when we mentioned we wanted to use the Dtac promos, they pushed back as if it was inconvenient for them and their attitude shifted! Shameful! || Great experience. Our seats were high up but don’t take the last one. You can’t push your seat all the way. The sound was amazing , the screen was great too. Sadly, our movie sucked. Superman was actually made for 12 year olds.  Definitely going back to watch Jurassic Park. || Staff disrespectful (one man and one lady) and refused to sell cold water. When I asked for ice they can’t even give me, I didn’t receive any apology or anything, can’t return the products as well Please make sure you know what they have in stock before buying || If you would like to have the experience in the excellent of seeing the good movies.  I recommend IMAX theater and the one at Emquartier. || This theatre is on the 4th floor of the mall. They have self serve kiosks to buy your own ticket as well. The upgraded seats were something like 350 baht which is a pretty good price for a bit more leg room and a bigger, comfier fabric chair.  The washrooms and premises in general are nice and clean and the theatre was ready to go in about ten minutes before the showtime. || Service 5/5  Parking 3 hours free  Good movie halls, we love watching movies here. Comfortable seats. Couple sofa seats are nice, also the single seats right below.  There is one hall which is excessively special (next to popcorn section). You get hot towels, champagne/ juice and some dry fruits. You can also order food. There is a buzzer to call them too. While bringing the juice the girl was walking on her knees. I deeply appreciate the service and the respect but we are all human, please treat us just like a normal human beings 🙏  2200 Baht for couple approximately || Large cinemas, comfortable seats, excellent sound system. Worth the ticket price. They do not sell hot drinks but allow you to buy Starbucks and bring the drinks into the cinema. Starbucks is located just outside the cinemas, really convenient and thoughtful. I'd you have children, you will be tempted to buy the popcorns since they come with nice containers you can bring home.

Suitable for activities with friends or loved ones on holidays. Food and drinks are available. The price of each game is 200 baht per person. There is also a shoe rental fee of 50 baht per person. || I recently visited Major Cineplex Sukhumvit for a movie night, and overall, I had a good experience. The theater has comfortable seating and the screen and sound quality really make the movie feel immersive. The selection of films is diverse enough whether you’re into big blockbusters or indie flicks. It can get a bit crowded during peak times, but that’s to be expected. Tourists like to take pictures. Taking pictures from across the road is very beautiful. || Phra Thinang Sutthaisawan Prasat is a royal residence located on the eastern wall of the Grand Palace, between the Thewa Phithak Gate and Sakchaisith Gate. King Rama I built this residence in 1784. Originally called "Phlap Phla Sung," it was later demolished and rebuilt between 1818 and 1827 by King Rama III, who ordered its demolition and reconstruction as a castle, naming it "Phra Thinang Sutthaisawan." King Rama IV restored it in 1853 and renamed it "Phra Thinang Sutthaisawan Prasat." He also designated it as one of the royal residences within the Phra Abhinavaniwet complex.  According to the Thai Encyclopedia for Youth, Phra Thinang Sutthaisawan Prasat is one of the royal residences within the Grand Palace. It is a palace built on a castle-like wall, located on the east side of the Grand Palace, between the Thewa Phithak Gate and Sakchaisith Gate. It features two sections of grandstands: the northern and southern grandstands, leading from the ground to the base. From the base, grandstands lead to the throne halls on the east, west, north, and south. The eastern side features a wooden gallery, built in 1949, serving as a balcony for the King to allow the public to pay their respects.  The Suthaisawan Prasat Throne Hall, originally called Phlap Phla Sung, was built during the reign of King Rama I to view the procession during the Grand Royal Ceremony, which included elephants, horses, and royal vehicles marching out to receive a sprinkling of holy water. This procession, also known as the Chaturongkasena Parade, involved foot soldiers, elephants, horses, and carriages. The procession passed in front of the throne hall to receive a sprinkling of holy water for auspiciousness and to observe elephant training. Later, during the reign of King Rama III, the palace was demolished and rebuilt in the style of a castle. and bestowed the name Phra Thinang Sutthasawan. Then, King Rama IV changed it to Phra Thinang Sutthaisawan Prasat. || Suthaisawan Prasat Throne Hall is located on Sanam Chai Road, opposite the Privy Council Building.  Flanking it are the Sakchaisith Gate and Thewapitak Gate. || Sutthaisawan Prasat Throne Hall is located on the eastern wall of the Grand Palace, between the Thewapitak Gate and the Sakchai Sitthichai Gate. This throne hall was built by King Rama I (Phra Phutthayotfa Chulalok) in 1784. Originally called "Phlabphla Sung" (High Pavilion), it was demolished and rebuilt as a palace between 1818 and 1827 by King Rama III (Phra Nangklao). He named it "Sutthaisawan Throne Hall." Later, King Rama IV (Phra Chomklao) renovated it in 1853 and renamed it "Sutthaisawan Prasat Throne Hall," placing it among the royal residences within the Grand Palace complex.  According to the Thai Encyclopedia for Youth, Sutthaisawan Prasat Throne Hall is one of the throne halls within the Grand Palace. The Sutthaisawan Palace is a castle-like structure situated on a wall on the eastern side of the Grand Palace, between the Thewa Phitak and Sakdi Chai Sitthichai gates. It has two levels of staircases: a northern and a southern staircase leading from the ground to the base. From the base, staircases lead up to the palace on the east, west, north, and south sides. On the eastern side is a wooden veranda built in 1949, serving as a royal balcony for the King to appear before the public.  The Sutthaisawan Palace, originally called the "High Pavilion," was built during the reign of King Rama I for viewing processions during the Grand Royal Ceremony of Sa Sanam Yai. This included the parade of elephants, horses, and royal vehicles to receive blessings with holy water, or a military parade consisting of infantry, elephants, horses, and chariots passing in front of the palace for auspicious blessings. It was also used to observe elephant training. Later, during the reign of King Rama III, it was demolished and rebuilt in the style of a palace. And it was given the name Phra Thinang Sutthasawan. Later, King Mongkut (Rama IV) changed it to Phra Thinang Sutthaisawan Prasat. They also provide guided tour with good English speaking guide. At the top floor, you can get a good panoramic view of Rama 8 suspension bridge and the old fort nearby. Highly recommend. || Impeccably maintained building and exhibits, highly educational tour and guide. They tell the story of the Treasury and also the history of the neighborhood, Bang Lamphu. The guide answered lots of other questions, too! || Everyone enjoy the exhibition either free admission at the first floor or buy the most cheapest ticket to join the tour group taking time traveller to the past almost century of Banglamphu, this area || A short walk from Phra Arthit Pier, passing by the Phra Sumen Fort and a row of shop houses. There are tours every half hour and the guides are lovely:) The first part of the tour introduces the government agency responsible for the development and maintenance of the museum. The second part - in a joint building - tells the history of the district, from its early market days to its multicultural community. || Nice museum for 30 THB entry. Note that the second floor (which is where most of the displays are) is only accessible with their guide. When I was there, it was 10.30 am when the tour started.  This building used to be a printing house before they converted it to a museum. Apparently every 17-19 December, they open the rooftop to the public.  Allocate at least an hour for the tour. Ground floor exhibits are for your viewing pleasure until the guide is available. You’re allowed to take photographs, but no videos. || Bang Lamphu Museum is located on Phra Sumen Road, and is walkable from Phra Artit Road.  The museum is quite local but surprising, the space seems to be one of my favorite museum in Thailand. Ticket price for docent to give us a 1 hour tour is only 30 Baht. The tour goes on every half an hour and each tour capacity is around 8-10 people at max.  Although the tour is based on Thai Language, the caption of some of the archaeological finds/items can be in English Description.  The museum shows us the fascinating story of Banglumphu old days where market selling and its district are what is known for. There's also history learning part on how land was developed from time to time and even how nickel/coin are crafted and used for from the old times.  An absolute wonderful museum that worth every penny. Some of the visitors (if his/her family member lives around here during 40s/50s) will surely inspired by those "nostalgic feeling" from start to the end.  Still photos are permitted only.

Great art exhibitions, along with displays on the history of Chulalongkorn University. There are also some coloring activities available. Admission is free. || A museum with huge potential. Sadly my expectations were crushed as all the information is written in Thai. If you are an English only person like me make sure you have google translate on your phone and your phone fully charged. || This musuem showcasing the university progress and development as well as world leaders who visiting Chula U previously || I visited the Chulalongkorn University Museum for the Butterflies & Cockroaches exhibit, which, while enjoyable, fell short of my expectations. I anticipated a more expansive or detailed presentation. On the other hand, the permanent exhibit, which showcases the foundational history and legacy of Chulalongkorn University, exceeded my admittedly modest expectations. Unfortunately, some sections of the main exhibit were closed for maintenance during my visit, which was slightly disappointing. Overall, the temporary exhibit was intriguing but could have offered more, while the permanent exhibit effectively highlighted the university's rich history, despite some areas being inaccessible. || One of the most amazingly well-thought-out place for a museum. It has a lot of exhibition areas, and the Centenary exhibition truly open up my eyes for the partial history of the university itself. || Good place to know about the university || Great place, great exhibition but hardly find the parking lot || Best university of Thailand with superb atmosphere with nature and wonderful architecture of auditorium .

Parutsakawan Palace is more than 100 years old. Nowadays this building is a museum with public access. The museum is open four days a week, from Tuesday to Friday. The museum is open from 10 AM to 4 PM. Entrance is free. This old palace is not well-known, but it is an interesting place to visit. || A hidden gem worth visiting! The villa is charming, and the Police Museum offers a fascinating insight into the history of the Thai police force. One of the highlights was learning about their work in border areas, where they engage ethnic Thai minorities in education and economic programs—an inspiring initiative that showcases their commitment beyond law enforcement. Best of all, entrance is completely free, making it an accessible and enriching experience for all visitors. Highly recommended for those interested in history, culture, and social development in Thailand! || This building is designed by an Italian architect, that’s the reason you could notice some Italian architecture elements in the building. The visitation is free of charge, and a detail tour explained by a friendly lady. I had a good time and gained a lot of insight. Strongly recommend! || There are two buildings to visit on this site, the more modern building houses the contents of the police museum and then you have the Chitralada Villa which for me was the highlight of my visit. Completed in 1906, it's beautifully designed. Heavily influenced by Italian architecture with Art Nouveau interior  and Baroque/Rococo influences. The police museum has various artifacts displayed aswell as a history of the changing structure of the police service over the centuries to create the service it provides today. Both buildings are totally free to visit, just register your name. || The Palace contains two parts - one part is Palace itself which is beautifully maintained and contains information regarding the Palace history and the Royal family.  The other part is Police Museum.  Both are free admission.  If more English translation is provided, it will be made the visit more interesting. || I wonder why the Police Museum named isn't mentioned in Google Map. The Palace part has no English and isn't big. Both aren't really big or very outstanding but since they are both different and you get to visit 2 attractions, it's still worth visiting. No lockers are provided and you need to take off your shoes. || This place was palace, now is used as police museum. If you expect the splendid palace like Emerald temple and Grand Palace, you are disappointed. However this place is very quiet and peaceful. When you don’t mind your limited travel time, I recommend this Police museum and former palace. || A fomer palace of Kind Rama v’s brother, now a police museum. Art nouveau is a rare type of architecture in Thailand, this place absolutely kills! Great architecture motifs with interesting history. The content of the museum is not much but the palace is really beautiful.  Not usually open for public, if there is a chance for you to visit, do not miss it. Admission is free, and there are parking lots nearby. || It’s combined of an old palace and a modern building. Fun fact about the police department. The staff there are really friendly. The garden is nice with ponds and stream surrounding the building. || Fantastic architecture, intricate ceilings . The modern building at the rear house the main museum.

Here some details, Clear entrance fee information. Foreigners: 300 THB for both museums or 200 THB for one. … || This was a good exhibit to see the folklore history of Thailand. The nice part is you can pay 300 baht and visit the anatomy museum, Siriraj medical museum, and Bimuksthan Museum. It's a great bargin! || A small museum which I find not worth coming if u are not traveling nearby. Some displays are not allowed to take pictures. Good for Thai primary schools kids to learn about medical stuff in olden Siam. || Very interesting museum that combines knowledge about medical history of Siriraj Hospital, on which premises it is currently located, old Railway station whose building it occupies, and the local district where it is located. || Very good experience for kid and myself to learn about Siriraj and also King. Good VDO presentation and anotomy || An excellent, well-designed museum despite a somewhat eclectic collection. Once you step inside from the beautiful pavilion outside, the museum’s guards will guide (some might say hustle) you through displays that start out displaying the … || It is an informative museum which tells about the history of Siriraj Hospital, the development of medicine and medical education in the historical context. It also gives information about the traditional Thai medicine which relies on … || Great museum displaying anything from medical and history of Thailand. Include the ancient boat found at the area. After visiting the museum, you can relax and enjoy beautiful Riverside park. || One entrance ticket allows you to visit various exhibitions which include history of Siriraj hospital, the old palace and medical surgery. The major attraction is the old large wooden boat which was excavated  and exhibited there. || This was a nice place to visit as was staying nearby and had a couple of hours to kill. It’s a large clean museum. Gives a good insight into this historical area of Bangkok as well as information about the history of the neighbouring …

Very nice place to visit. Enjoying good art in a/c room is the best.  Even on I day I went there only 2 rooms have exhibition held. || The main building is closed for renovation. They asked 240 B to see two temporary exhibits. I did not do this. They sent me across the road (walk under the bridge thru subway construction) to a gallery at Wangna Theatre (see attached photo). I am not sure this is what they intended for me to see, but it is a free gallery with mediocre art. || Only 2 of 4 halls were open when I visited. There were some of the most inspiring and creative pieces that I have seen in a long time. The work reflects my impression of Thailand... surprising, innovative, fun, and unexpected. Loved it, except I wanted more! || 7/8/25 - Almost all of the exhibition rooms/ buildings are closed for maintenance work until end of 2025. Only two exhibition rooms are available. So, please check before visiting. || Wonderful exhibition today for a single artist.  Dozens of paintings displaying  his many works and artistic styles over the years.  Standing back you would not think the same artist painted them all.  A very well done exhibition of artistic talent.  The artist is pictured here.  The rest of the museum is closed for renovations. || The National Gallery is a short walk around the corner from several other parks and museums. For only 30 Baht, visitors get access to main spaces that are open as well as the sculpture garden. Visitors should not pay anymore than 30 Baht either in advance or online. They do a lot of repairs and recirculating, so everything is not always open... With that said, we had a chance to see local artists and a Thai professor's exhibition. There is a timeline of past artists influenced by Western culture as well as a welcome from King Rama IX. Overall it's worth an hour and a half of your time. Families will love the expanse, shade and air conditioned exhibits and picnic area at the National Gallery. || Difficult to get to and underwhelming. The gallery appears to shut randomly without notice, so don’t make any special journeys in hopes of seeing it unless you call ahead to ensure it’ll be open when you arrive. The old mint and its courtyard offer a great venue to appreciate Bangkok’s 19th century, European-inspired architecture and the art therein. But not really worth the 200 baht admission. So stop in if you happen to be in the area, but don’t go out of your way. (Btw, pics allowed with no flash) || Open to the public with a 200THB admission fee.  Hosting several exhibitions including the BAB2024.. The venue is close to major other museums and sights.   Mobility assistance is offered but might need the support of staff if required to operate some lifts. Well worth a visit if art is your thing. || I can't say that this gallery is completely unworthy of the time and money spent, but I was a bit disappointed.  The painting collection is weak, and there are only four rooms open for visitors.  Across the road from this gallery, there is a National museum that is ten times more interesting and larger. And the admission fee is the same 200 thb. || The National Gallery of Bangkok 🇹🇭 Located on Chao Fa Road in Bangkok’s historic Phra Nakhon District and is housed in the building of the former Royal Thai Mint. You will see unknown and renowned Thai artworks here, both old and new.  Great place for a rainy day, that’s not a shopping mall 🛍️  Give yourself at least 1 hour here.  Ticket cost 200 baht ($6 USD) Open Wednesday – Sunday, 9am – 4pm  Directly across the street is The National Museum. Easy and convenient to see both in the same day (also 200baht ticket).

I recently visited MYTH Apothecary Spa after reading several positive reviews and seeing the elegant photos online. The place definitely looks impressive — from the moment you step inside, you can tell that a lot of care and attention has gone into creating a calm, luxurious atmosphere. The reception area is beautifully decorated, the aroma in the air is relaxing, and the staff greets you with warmth and professionalism. Everything about the environment says “high-end,” and in that regard, the spa absolutely delivers.  I decided to try their Siamese Massage, which is one of their signature treatments and also one of the most expensive on the menu. The total cost was 1,500 baht for 90 minutes, which is quite high compared to most massage places in Thailand. Still, I was curious to see whether the experience would justify the price.  The massage itself was good — relaxing, clean, and professional. The therapist clearly knew what she was doing and maintained excellent technique throughout the session. However, in terms of the actual massage experience, it didn’t feel drastically different from the traditional Thai massages I’ve had elsewhere during my trip. I’ve been in Thailand for about ten days and have been getting massages almost every day, so I’ve had plenty to compare it to. The Siamese Massage at MYTH felt like a standard Thai massage with a few small extras — some oil, smoother transitions between techniques, and maybe a bit more attention to detail in the stretching and pressure points. But overall, it wasn’t an experience that stood out dramatically from the rest.  What really sets this place apart is the setting and the facilities, not the massage itself. Everything is spotless — the rooms are comfortable, the sheets smell fresh, the lighting is soft and relaxing, and every corner of the spa feels perfectly maintained. You can tell this is a 5-star environment, and you’re paying for that. The location also plays a big part: it’s in a premium area where everything tends to cost more, and that’s clearly reflected in the pricing.  If what you’re looking for is a luxury spa experience with a high level of comfort and top-notch service, then MYTH Apothecary Spa is a great choice. You’ll feel pampered and relaxed in a beautiful setting. But if what you really care about is just getting an excellent massage, you can easily find something very similar elsewhere for a third of the price.  So while I did enjoy my time here and left feeling relaxed, I can’t say the massage itself was worth the premium cost. It’s a nice experience overall, but in my opinion, 1,500 baht for this treatment is simply too much. || Had an amazing experience here! The staff were very welcoming, the atmosphere was clean and relaxing, and my therapist really listened to what I needed. I walked out feeling so much lighter and refreshed. Highly recommend if you’re looking for a professional and relaxing massage || After a long flight from Europe, I was looking for a high-quality massage close to where I was staying, in the Ari neighborhood. The place is easy to reach on foot from my hostel, so I decided to try it and chose the first treatment on the menu: a 1-hour massage including a foot massage (45 minutes) and head and shoulders (15 minutes) for 750 THB (around €20).  I always check reviews before booking, and this spa had excellent ones. I can now say I was not disappointed at all.  Yes, it is more expensive than the typical Thai massage places you can find nearby, but honestly, you would never get something of this quality for that price in France.  The place itself is beautiful, a little oasis in the middle of a busy city. Everything is clean and well maintained. The staff speak some English and are very respectful, no phone calls during the massage, no loud conversations. You are welcomed with a cold drink, the air conditioning is comfortable, you remove your shoes and they provide a clean pair for you. The toilets are also spotless.  There is soft jazz background music, played at just the right volume, and you have your own private cabin, which really adds to the feeling of calm and intimacy. This is clearly not a cheap, rushed massage experience, but a thoughtful and well-designed one.  The massage itself was a very authentic Thai massage. I especially appreciated that the therapist respected my request for a gentler pressure. It helped a lot with blood circulation after a long flight and deeply relaxed my head and shoulders. Seeing the care she put into the head work, I would actually recommend choosing a longer head massage next time.  The treatment ends with a small refreshment, a hot drink and some sweets, which is a lovely final touch. Payment is easy, either by cash or card at the front desk.  I would absolutely recommend this place and would happily come back. || Absolutely loved the atmosphere here. It’s calm, cosy, and just what I needed for a laid-back kind of day. The staff were so warm and attentive, and the massage was simply amazing. Everything from the soothing ambience to the thoughtful service made the experience feel truly relaxing. Highly recommend this spot to anyone looking to unwind and recharge. || This detached garden villa in Ari, Bangkok, is nestled amidst lush greenery, offering a tranquil and relaxing atmosphere. The service and prices are also very reasonable🧚🏼 … || Such an amazing experience. Beautiful and cozy environment and I would definitely come back again!hidden gem in Bangkok. My first spa and definitely recommend it || This is a true hidden gem! From the moment I stepped into this charming spa housed in a traditional Thai bungalow, I felt an immediate sense of calm and tranquility.  We were taken to a beautifully appointed couple’s room featuring full-length windows — we requested to keep the curtains open with only the sheer, and the soft sunlight streaming in made the experience even more soothing.  The therapists were experienced, delivering a deeply relaxing 1.5-hour hot stone and oil massage in perfect harmony.  Afterwards, we lingered a bit longer in the cozy lounge area, sipping on a comforting cup of hot tea — the perfect way to ease back into the world. || It’s the best you can do for your mind and body. Absolutely charming garden and house, everybody is so kind and the place is very clean. You have to fill out a form before the massage so you can explain what you want and then you just have to relax during your session. Also delicious tea before and after the massage. The masseuse really paid attention to details : lightening, temperature of the room, covers you with blanket + covers your eyes for a deeper relaxation. Just perfect ! I recommend this place 100% It’s the best you can do to recharge your batteries in a city like Bangkok. I’ll come back again ! || Absolutely insanity precisely cure my iron leg and neck. Not that kinda strong pushing but every beat dropped on the right spot. Will definitely come back again || I had a wonderful relaxing Massage in this place. It feels like a small little oasis and the staff is extremely friendly. I would definitely come back!

This Thai massage centre offers one of the best massage experiences in Bangkok. The atmosphere is calm and welcoming from the moment you walk in, and the staff are attentive, professional, and genuinely skilled. A special mention goes to Perry, the therapist, whose technique was exceptional and made the entire session deeply relaxing and truly rejuvenating. She maintained the perfect balance of pressure and rhythm, easing tension while still keeping the massage soothing and enjoyable from start to finish.  The aroma massage with medium pressure was an excellent choice. The experience begins with selecting your preferred oils and scrubs, allowing you to personalise the treatment to your liking.  The thoughtfulness continue after the session. Guests are offered a refreshing green tea and a small cookie, adding a comforting finish to the experience. The centre is impressively clean, hygienic, and well-maintained, which enhances the overall sense of comfort and professionalism.  Overall, this place delivers outstanding service, skilled therapists, and a peaceful environment. With therapists like Perry providing such high-quality care, it truly stands out. A full five-star experience and highly recommended for anyone looking for a top-tier massage in Bangkok. || I had the most incredible essential oil massage here today! The therapist had expert hands that melted away weeks of tension. She carefully selected a calming lavender blend and adjusted the pressure perfectly. The room was beautifully serene with soft music and warm lighting. I left feeling completely rejuvenated, both in body and mind. The entire experience was worth every penny. This is my new go-to spot for self-care. Highly recommended! || One hidden gem in the middle of Bangkok city. I had one of the best Aromatic massage with Tee. She has excellent hand movements techniques that make the knots melted away with the right pressure. The music and ambient is peaceful and clean, the cold tower in the beginning and the hot towel in the end is very sensational! I highly recommended this place. || Great experience. Clean, calming, friendly and most importantly: a good massage (10/10). You will come out feeling refreshed and lighter.  I stayed nearby and came here a few times. Would definitely come back. || LOVED my foot massage so much! They also did my legs and at the end shoulders/neck. My first time I did a massage and it definitely won’t be my laste one here. The salon also looks very nice, modern en clean. I recommend! :) || Booked a Thai Balm massage 90 minutes, wow amazing ladies. Beautiful and professional massage palour, great price. Worth a visit if staying at The Unicorn building, Eastern Grand hotel or Phaya Thai area (BTS). 2 min from the hotel || I walked into Thyme House when it opened—it’s super close to my hotel and easy to find. The space is clean and peaceful, and the 2-hour Thai massage was just what I needed. The therapist was skilled, with just the right pressure throughout. Best of all, the price is very reasonable. || My husband and I loved this place so much that we visited twice during our 3-day trip to Bangkok. The Thai balm massage was incredible—firm, rejuvenating, and perfect for tired muscles. On our second visit, we tried the aromatic oil massage, which was wonderfully calming, and the coconut cream left our skin unbelievably soft. Thank you for such a memorable experience. We’ll truly miss this place! || “The first time I came in by accident, but then I started visiting intentionally. It’s a good salon: clean, smells nice, the staff wear uniforms and have proper equipment. The staff behave professionally. The skill level is good. The price is reasonable. I recommend it.” || After shopping and exploring around Bangkok for a few days, my whole body was really sore, especially my arms. I just randomly came across this massage shop, and it turned out to be the best massage I’ve ever had. They have the most professional masseuses, they really know what they’re doing and addressed all my main concerns. One of the best experiences I’ve had in Bangkok!

Amazing experience at Calm Spa! Concierge Aof and Mimi were very friendly and welcoming. I did the 90-minute signature oil massage with Lampai — it was so relaxing and absolutely worth every penny. The post-massage snacks were delicious too! Highly recommend! 🙌✨ … || 🙏🏼 Greetings from Calm Spa Thailand  Thank you so much for your 5 stars rating and sharing your wonderful spa experience with us !  It’s always our pleasure to be at your service  Have a calming and beautiful day 🙏🏻😊 || Always love coming to Calm Spa, but this was my first time meeting Khun Mimi at the front desk. She’s so friendly and attentive, helped explain the menu and share great promos. The whole experience was relaxing from start to finish, and the snacks before and after the treatment were absolutely delicious. Left feeling calm, pampered, and already looking forward to my next visit! || Thank you very much for sharing your wonderful experience with us.  We look forward to welcoming you back again soon for another relaxing moment at Calm Spa Thailand ✨ || Calm Spa is my absolute favorite spa in Bangkok, it’s my second time visit here. We look forward to welcoming you back again soon for another relaxing moment at Calm Spa Thailand ✨ || Calm Spa Ari is a welcoming place with a very good reception Ms Mimi who can speak very good English and familiar with their products. The message therapists Lampai and Aree are professional and attentive. || Thank you very much for sharing your wonderful experience with us.  We look forward to welcoming you back again soon for another relaxing moment at Calm Spa Thailand ✨ || I absolutely love the atmosphere at this spa – it’s so relaxing and inviting from the moment you walk in. Great experience. || SF Cinema at MBK Mall is a serviceable theater that does the job but doesn’t impress. It’s better than Paragon Cineplex, but falls short of other SF locations like Central World or Central Rama 9. The sound and screens are decent, the seats are fine, but it lacks the staff attentiveness, style, and thoughtful design choices that separate a good theater from a great one. If you're already at MBK and want to catch a movie, it’s a passable option—just don’t expect anything special. 3/5.  Full Review SF Cinema at MBK Mall is a middle-of-the-road theater experience—not bad, not great, just fine. If you’re already at MBK and looking to watch a movie, it’ll get the job done, but if you have the chance to go elsewhere, you probably should.  Comparisons: A Theater That Falls in the Middle Compared to Paragon Cineplex, it’s leagues ahead, simply because it manages to maintain basic standards of cleanliness, functionality, and service. However, when put up against SF Cinema locations like Central World or even Central Rama 9, it falls behind. It lacks the polish, premium feel, and staff efficiency that make those locations shine.  Screen, Sound & Seating: Just Okay The screen and sound quality are fair—not cutting-edge, but not distracting either. If you’re just looking for a functional cinema experience, it’s fine. However, don’t expect the kind of deep bass, sharp projection, or immersive surround sound you’d get at a premium location.  The seats are comfy enough for the duration of a film, but they don’t stand out. It’s the kind of seating that works but isn’t particularly memorable—no plush recliners, no extra comfort perks, just standard cinema seats.  Atmosphere & Service: Missing the Extra Touches This is where the theater falters the most. There’s no sense of identity or style—nothing about the design, the lobby, or the overall ambiance makes it feel special. It lacks the subtle details that elevate a theater-going experience, whether that’s a well-designed lounge area, a strong concessions lineup, or a staff that goes the extra mile to enhance the visit.  While the staff are generally competent, they don’t stand out as particularly welcoming or proactive. It’s a get-in, watch-your-movie, and leave kind of place, rather than a destination theater experience.  Final Verdict: Decent, But Forgettable SF Cinema at MBK Mall is a perfectly average theater. If you’re in the area and need a place to watch a movie, it’s a safe enough choice, but there’s nothing compelling enough to make it worth going out of your way for. It’s clean, functional, and better than some of the truly bad theaters out there, but it doesn’t have the polish, service, or premium feel of better SF locations.  If convenience is your priority, this will do. A solid 3/5 experience, this theater gets the basics right while leaving room for improvement. Depending on your preferences and budget, it might be worth a visit—but don’t set your expectations too high.  For smaller movies shown on their standard screens, the experience is, unfortunately, lackluster. The image projection and sound systems feel a bit underwhelming, especially if you’ve been spoiled by more premium setups elsewhere. Additionally, sound bleeding from neighboring auditoriums was noticeable during quieter moments, which detracted from the overall immersion. While these issues won’t ruin your experience, they are enough to warrant some disappointment for cinephiles who expect better technical performance.  The Zigma Cinestadium, however, elevates the experience. With enhanced sound and image quality, it offers a far more engaging way to enjoy bigger blockbusters or visually driven films. The increased price tag is something to consider, but for those who value presentation, it’s a worthwhile splurge.  The First Class option, while pricey, is another decent feature. It’s not just about the improved viewing experience but also the added perks that make it feel more indulgent. A separate bathroom for the VIP-like area is a thoughtful touch, ensuring convenience and exclusivity. The service here is also notably better than in standard screenings, and while not flawless, it’s a step up. The food on offer was decent—nothing extraordinary, but satisfying enough to complement the premium experience.  The theater overall is clean and well-maintained, and the layout is functional, if unremarkable. However, the cinema’s varying quality means your experience will largely depend on which screening option you choose. If you’re on a budget, the standard screenings might feel subpar, especially with soundproofing issues. On the other hand, if you’re willing to invest in Zigma or First Class, you’ll find more to enjoy.  SFX Cinema Central Rama 9 is decent but far from stellar. It gets the job done for casual moviegoers but won’t leave a lasting impression on those who seek the best cinematic experience. There are loads of different stalls serving different dishes to suit everyone.  The food is fantastic, many of the dishes will be made to order right in front of you and come out piping hot.   The pricing is outstanding too, you'll find a lot of the Thai classics for more on the street.  I know some purists will say that it's not as good as what you'll get on the street, that is likely true in some cases but there are plenty of times what you get on the street is not great at all.    We came several times over the past week and it is always busy with tourists and locals.  I highly recommend you check it out, especially for tourists who are a little hesitant to be introduced to Thai cuisine on the street.  This is a clean environment to try a number of great dishes. || The value for money is amazing. Super cheap (meals cost about 1 dollar) and you can wander around and choose whatever you like. Foodwise, it is almost entirely Asian cuisine but the quality was good, portions were slightly small but cannot complain at these prices. Try the masaman curry... delicious! You can also get takeaway which I did several times and heated it up the next day in the microwave in my hotel room. Only negatives are that it is always packed. Full Review SF Cinema at MBK Mall is a middle-of-the-road theater experience—not bad, not great, just fine. If you’re already at MBK and looking to watch a movie, it’ll get the job done, but if you have the chance to go elsewhere, you probably should.  Comparisons: A Theater That Falls in the Middle Compared to Paragon Cineplex, it’s leagues ahead, simply because it manages to maintain basic standards of cleanliness, functionality, and service. However, when put up against SF Cinema locations like Central World or even Central Rama 9, it falls behind. It lacks the polish, premium feel, and staff efficiency that make those locations shine.  Screen, Sound & Seating: Just Okay The screen and sound quality are fair—not cutting-edge, but not distracting either. If you’re just looking for a functional cinema experience, it’s fine. However, don’t expect the kind of deep bass, sharp projection, or immersive surround sound you’d get at a premium location.  The seats are comfy enough for the duration of a film, but they don’t stand out. It’s the kind of seating that works but isn’t particularly memorable—no plush recliners, no extra comfort perks, just standard cinema seats.  Atmosphere & Service: Missing the Extra Touches This is where the theater falters the most. There’s no sense of identity or style—nothing about the design, the lobby, or the overall ambiance makes it feel special. It lacks the subtle details that elevate a theater-going experience, whether that’s a well-designed lounge area, a strong concessions lineup, or a staff that goes the extra mile to enhance the visit.  While the staff are generally competent, they don’t stand out as particularly welcoming or proactive. It’s a get-in, watch-your-movie, and leave kind of place, rather than a destination theater experience.  Final Verdict: Decent, But Forgettable SF Cinema at MBK Mall is a perfectly average theater. If you’re in the area and need a place to watch a movie, it’s a safe enough choice, but there’s nothing compelling enough to make it worth going out of your way for. It’s clean, functional, and better than some of the truly bad theaters out there, but it doesn’t have the polish, service, or premium feel of better SF locations. Very good theater. I saw the Phantom of the Opera inside, it’s absolutely amazing. Except the theater itself is a little bit small for the show. Esplanade, ground floor offers an amazing variety of restaurants and a smaller (but perfectly adequate) Tops store. A striking difference to the popular massive  malls is the lack of tourists, it’s as if Esplanade has escaped the attention of the hordes of visitors. Besides the impressive selection of   restaurants, Esplanade offers so much  more from an entertainment perspective. A bowling 🎳 alley with pool tables, karaoke 🎤 and a bar, a cinema 🎦, and easy access to THE ONE RACHADA night market… which opens at 5pm. || This is a good mall just by a station. Modern and energetic!! You can find nice delis, cafes and restaurants!! There are mini market in the ground floor it looks nice! It’s famous here for great view of Train night market from 4th floor’s car parking!! First of all you would feel confused but just go up to 4th floor by the escalator then maybe other tourists who have same purpose are around here and they are heading to same direction! So catch up them then you can get in at the point!!! Enjoy!! || Staffs are friendly and heloful. The floor to buy ticket and cinema are on a different floors. Plenty of machine and staffs on site. I dont usually come here but they have good movies showing. The popular Ritfai market is out back behind this mall. Modern clean facility with several theaters, including an Imax. Seats are soft, comfortable, and recline, sound system is clear and loud, but not run at ear-piercing levels. The IMAX theater here is new, clean, and well-maintained. The staff are always friendly and provide great service every time I visit.  To be honest, I actually find the overall system and experience here even smoother than at Paragon. It's also way less crowded, which makes the whole experience much more enjoyable.  During major movie releases, they often decorate the Box Office zone nicely or give out small goodies, which is a fun touch.  While some large-scale events or promotions may not be as big as what Paragon offers, this place is improving steadily and it’s definitely worth supporting. || The Management should regularly audit and anonymously review the service!  Staff on their phones while on duty (not just one but two of them)! Also when we mentioned we wanted to use the Dtac promos, they pushed back as if it was inconvenient for them and their attitude shifted! Shameful! || Great experience. Our seats were high up but don’t take the last one. You can’t push your seat all the way. The sound was amazing , the screen was great too. Sadly, our movie sucked. The upgraded seats were something like 350 baht which is a pretty good price for a bit more leg room and a bigger, comfier fabric chair. You get hot towels, champagne/ juice and some dry fruits. You can also order food. There is a buzzer to call them too. While bringing the juice the girl was walking on her knees. I deeply appreciate the service and the respect but we are all human, please treat us just like a normal human beings 🙏  2200 Baht for couple approximately || Large cinemas, comfortable seats, excellent sound system. place_name: Sodsai Pantoomkomol Centre for Dramatic Arts, Chulalongkorn University
reviews_content: It's located on the 6th floor of MahaChakkri Sirinthron building, faculty of Arts,  Chulalongkorn University. This is a good black box theatre. Wanted to try the Thai cinema experience. It did not disappoint! VERY clean place, seats are super comfy (took the exclusive pair, 800 thb for 2) and the sound is actually amazing in there even if it's one of their smaller room. The negative part is not about the place itself, but the Thai malls in general as they usually have absolutely NO map inside (pretty much all of them!), like we walked for ages until we decided to get into a random elevator and saw "SFX Cinema, 6th floor" on the floors panel. Popcorn and refreshments are also there (another counter) and prices are friendly. || Enjoyed the first class cinema. Ticket price is THB1,100 per person and comes with popcorn, light snacks and drinks.  Sevice is friendly and efficient.  Worth the visit for the special movie. || located on the top floor of Central ladprao shopping more in Bangkok, i brought a ticketet of captain Marvel for 240bath I'm not sure but I think it's a bit more expensive than Major ciniplex, somehow, overall are great environmental, seating area and sound are showing great performance. it's busy during the weekend || Huge Cinema Complex with a pretty nice waiting area.

Never in my life have I experienced service like this. Truly a VIP experience. The best caramel popcorn delivered to your seat. A lounge are where you are offered tea/coffee. Complimentary nibbles (and by nibbles I mean a chocolate fountain!!) while you wait for your showtime. A mini fridge stocked with drinks beside your lounge. Oh and someone brought my friend a blanket in case her legs got too cold from the AC. || Yes it is quite pricey BUT worth trying once. I didn’t have time to get a snacks plate before the movie, and couldn’t change my mind to go get some during the movie because the movie was too good to miss out on.  I also did not like at all that pop corn and soft drinks are NOT included in the ticket price. You would think those are snacks that should be in the snack bar, right?
