The service is exceptional, the lounge feels like a 5-star hotel, and the seats are actually flat beds with pillows and blankets – pure comfort! Picture and sound quality are outstanding, and the option to enjoy gourmet food and drinks makes the whole experience unforgettable. Worth every baht if you want to treat yourself to the best movie experience in the city. || Very nice theater. Plush seats and decor in the waiting area reminded me of a San Francisco Hotel called the Fairmont Hotel. Classy luxurious and easily a place to bring and impress your friends. Once you purchase your tickets you are invited to the array of snacks i.e. fried chicken mushroom over crackers and your choice of many more and alcoholic treats. The fried chicken is tender and moist. Very good. You can order beverages and have them delivered to your seat. So with temptation I had a nice glass of Merlot to sip during my view of the film  Bruitist. A 3 hour really 4 hour movie of a Jewish man, an architect who goes through the hardship establishing work when landing in America, dealing with prejudice, a boss who takes advantage of him in many ways and a wife who has to tolerate his vices. The theater has director chairs which recline almost to a lie-flat but are comfortable. They supply a silk blanket in case you’re cold or want an extra pillow behind your head. Overall a really nice place to go, have drinks, bring your friends and see a movie if your choice. Highly recommended! || We have an amazing experience. The cinema looks luxurious. The "bed-like" flatseat was very comfortable. The service was fantastic. Welcome drink and food at the snack bar was very good. There's a mini bar next to the seat too. We will definitely visit again next time when we travel to bangkok. || For 2 people for bed cinema experience was AUD $180 , honestly was not worth the price.  We got there at 9pm and movie started at 9.45pm (venom) we had time to get a few complimentary tiny snacks - they had been sitting there for a while so nothing was fresh.  Disappointing for the price to say the least.  They could have more options for food and drinks provided within the cost.  The workers just stand there staring at you when you’re trying to help yourself with the food and drinks making it awkward and not wanting to get anything.  The bed cinema experience itself was amazing and comfortable I will definitely do it again but somewhere else —  The mini fridge next to us only had 2x small chocolate bars and a few drinks they said we had complimentary beers inside but nothing was in the fridge.  Overall I would rate the bed cinema experience 6/10 || This cinema is amazing with very high quality seats, beds, food and drinks, and amazing staff. I was recommended this cinema by Brace, one of your workers, and he wasnt wrong about how good this place is. This cinema has very well done and high quality seats that were really comfortable and nice. The beds were well made and very comfortable. I like the beds very much because I can get 𝓯𝓻𝓮𝓪𝓴𝔂 with the person I’m going with. place_name: Sala Chaloem Thani - an old theatre
reviews_content: Yes!!! Only two days to see, enjoy and share an historical moment! This old theater is finally reopened and show a few movies to commemorate this old dreams… starting with the Frères Lumiere today. A wooden structure, a scream and a community… this is it! || Very interesting to watch old movies in a retro atmosphere. Also there is picturesque community built around it. || The oldest cinema in Bangkok || A building with a fascinating history - but there is nothing much more here || A historical landmark of Thai cinema, this 107-year-old wooden cinema, the first of its kind in Thailand, first opened in 1918 (during the reign of King Rama VI). It screened silent 16mm films with live dubbing. The large, two-story wooden building had no central pillars and a wooden roof with a corrugated iron roof. Initially named "Nang Loeng Cinema," it was renamed "Sala Chalermthani" in 1932 to align with other "Chalerm" chain cinemas such as Sala Chalermkrung and Sala Chalermthai. It closed and became a warehouse in 1993, operating for a remarkable 75 years. A major renovation took place in 2019-2020 to allow for the screening of classic films and to establish it as a landmark of the Nang Loeng area.  Currently, various events are regularly held at the cinema. Most recently, on "World Film Day" (December 27-28, 2025), the Thai Film Archive (Public Organization) screened a collection of classic films, from pioneering French films like Lumiere! to the silent comedy Laurel & Hardy and live-dubbed Thai films. Mae Nak Phra Khanong, 1959 version || I'm so happy to see you alive again 🤎 It's so heartwarming. … || The last remaining wooden stand-alone cinema in Bangkok is located behind Nang Loeng Market. It has been restored and renovated to look stronger than before, but it is still not open to the public. || The exterior is very beautiful. It is very well preserved. || The stand-alone cinema has long since closed, but it still retains its unique architectural structure. || Nang Loeng Cinema was built during the reign of King Rama VI by the Phatthanakan Film Company. It was one of the earliest cinemas in Thailand, having its premiere on December 18, 1918. The business was later sold to Saha Cinema Co., Ltd., under the Crown Property Bureau, during the reign of King Rama VII, during the 150th anniversary of Bangkok. The name was changed to Sala Chalerm Thani to align with the other seven cinemas, which began with the word “Chalerm,” namely Sala Chalermkrung, Sala Chalermthai, Sala Chalerm Nakhon, Sala Chalermburi, Sala Chalerm Wiang, Sala Chalerm Rat, and Sala Chalerm Rat.

No trip to Bangkok is complete unless you eat the street food and some of my favorites can be found here. You'd need a prodigious appetite and a capacity to match if your intention is to try half of the stalls in one sitting, so it would be a good idea to visit over a couple of meals ( or even a couple of days if you intend to include Silom's back alley sois nearby which are also lined with street stalls during lunch ).  One of my favorite stalls is the fried dumplings that come with several choices of filling. Similar to the Teochew soon kway (which is normally steamed), this glutinous dumpling is instead fried in a shallow pan of oil to a crisp and served with a sweet black soy sauce. My favorite fillings are either the steamed chives or bamboo shoots. Great as a starter as you make your way down the street to try the heavier stuff (all of which are thankfully light on the wallet) ! || Tried Tokyo and coconut cake here, tokyos soft and blend, not crispy, coconut cakes not delicious as well, maybe try other food next time. || Tried omelette rice where you can choose your ingredients and chicken wings, the chili sauce is so special. Other food too. || So many delicious foods on offer. Recommend the banana coconut pancake. || Restaurant Yellorice. We had a very good and unforgetable experience. Very good food, great service and honest price! || This fried banana shop is good … very crispy and tasty 👍 30 baht per set || Great chicken and rice meal (80 baht, extra large) beside a busy road. || Not very long street stalk about 15 stalls, || A lot of delicious food on this street from morning till night || Papaya Chicken salad must try!

place_name: That little Thai Street Food Place
ノーイおばさんのガパオライス
reviews_content: Perfect breakfast! Rice with egg. 🍳 Loved it. || I arrived around 8:50 AM on November 23, 2025. It supposedly opens at 9 AM, so I wondered where Auntie Noi's stall was, and just as I was passing by, I was greeted by Auntie Noi, asking, "Would you like some gapao rice?"  There were some adorable moments, like when she overcooked an egg and laughed 😂 The unique atmosphere of a food stall was great, and they even adjusted the spiciness for me, giving the gapao rice a nostalgic taste. I ordered, ate, and paid 60 baht. The convenience of only being there in about 15 minutes is one of the great things about food stalls! Thank you! || It's just an ordinary little food stall, but for some reason it seems to be quite popular and well-known. I was curious, so I went there with a bit of a trendy attitude.  The menu seems to have a variety of options, but it's only in Thai, so I decided to order gapow rice.  Once you order, Auntie Noi skillfully and leisurely prepares your dish.  This time I had "Pad Gapao Moo Sap Kai Dao (Pad Gapao Moo Sap Kai Dao)." It's gapow rice with moo sap (minced pork). I also added a Kai Dao (fried egg). My friend wasn't feeling well, so I asked for it to be less spicy, which was just right for Japanese palates. The rich flavor and moderate spiciness were delicious. It was even better when mixed with a soft-boiled egg. The basil stems, which aren't often included in other restaurants, are fried until they're crisp and delicious.  Well, it's just an ordinary food stall, but if it's this delicious, it's bound to become popular. It makes you want to try their other dishes too. || This stall is run by a friendly and affable lady all by herself.  Naturally, the gapow is delicious, and best of all, it's cheap!  The nearest station is Phrom Phong, but it's about a 30-minute walk, so it's best to take a motorbike taxi or motorbike taxi. || The gapow (60B) here has absolutely no unpleasant taste or odor from the ingredients, and has a really clear and gentle flavor that is absolutely amazing ♪ Auntie, take care 🌹 || I went to eat Gapao rice because the reviews were good. There are several food stalls lined up on the sidewalk, and this is one of them. To be honest, the taste wasn't bad, but it wasn't as good as everyone said it was. I still preferred eating at Pier 21. It's a Thai food stall with a nice atmosphere. It's a bit far to walk, so it's better to go by motorbike taxi. || It was very delicious✨The price is reasonable✨They will adjust the spiciness if you ask. || I wanted to eat gapao rice at a food stall, so I went to Auntie Noi's gapao rice. I ordered gapao moo sap kai dao. There were several food stalls lined up, so it was a little difficult to find, but Auntie Noi welcomed me with a smile! The taste of the gapao rice was impeccable, the classic gapao rice! || The spiciness is mild, but just right for Japanese people. It's packed with meat and, above all, has an intense flavor that will have you eating your spoonful! It was unexpectedly delicious for an open-air restaurant stall. 60 baht (¥250) for a pissé (large portion) is a bargain. || The gapow rice here has large portions of stir-fried meat, is just the right amount of spicy, and the rice and ingredients mix well together, making it very easy to eat. I would even order a large portion of rice and two fried eggs lol. The staff seem to be used to foreigners, as they asked me as soon as I arrived, "Is this gapow?" The location is for advanced customers, but if you follow the introduction video on YouTube, you'll be sure to find it. If you're going to Bangkok, I highly recommend giving it a try. m(__)m

Recommend you all to try this || The bami kiao (wanton noodles) was  acceptable but unremarkable. It tasted okay, but there was nothing special or memorable about the taste. The chicken was similarly average. Can visit only if you’re at the vicinity of thong lo/ Phrom phong as the price is quite affordable || Meeting ran long, missed lunch… now all I can think about is a bowl of amazing noodles … || Tasty old school vibes 🎉 Stumbled upon this charming old-school eatery while staying nearby, and it turned out to be a great find! I was there for brunch and ordered their chicken rice, crispy pork, and longan juice—each dish was delicious … || A famous chicken rice shop with a long history. A simple set up shop with limited seatings and can be crowded during peak hours.  Not the best chicken rice that I had but definitely one of the better one around. Rice and chicken were nicely cook and delicious! || Old school family style chicken rice & noodle spot with fish meatballs & others. Right on Sukhumvit road. Fast and easy, order right when you walk in. Get the black sauce when you order the chicken rice and try the yen ta fo (fermented tofu red sauce fish noodle soup) with sen yai (big noodle). || Delicioussssss! Simple but so good. The chicken is tender and the rice is aromatic and so tasty. Can’t go wrong with that or the pork over rice. The noodle soups are also fantastic, especially the red one. Service is super friendly and accommodating. They don’t speak much English but they’re amazing. Love it. || The best family food shop in the neighborhood! Fish ball noodles? Right on point. Chicken rice? Wonderful, especially the sauce. Crispy pork? Dayummm. Chicken and crispy pork combined on rice? Heavenly!!! … || A shop with old traditional feels.  The soup noodle was spicy & sour & savoury with crispy dumplings, balls, blood cube etc.... for THB$60. LongGan drink was great at THB$10.

This place serves very delicious, no frills, nothing fancy, staple Thai food. If you want to experience true local dinning then come here. Location is very convenient, only a 5 minute walk from Sukhumvit on Soi 23. Try every dish they offer and find what you like.  My favorite is their grapao muu. || I am rating the whole experience a 4 out of 5. The service was great, the egg was perfect, the rice could be better. I would appreciate the dish more if the rice was hot. Maybe if I visit again I would try the chicken. The ground pork was a bit tough for my preference. || Saved this place for almost 2 years now. Didn't have the opportunity to try this place on my last 2 trips to Bangkok. The hotel I happen to stay for this trip is actually very near to this place. I decided to go check this out since it was the last day in Bangkok. I was there around late 11am  and there wasn't any crowd.  The elderly cook and the service staff were very friendly. The menu has both English and Chinese, so it was easy to understand. Ordered the basil chicken rice and a bottle of Pepsi. Food didn't take long to be ready.  Food didn't disappoint as expected. Food was well seasoned and can taste wok hei. In total, I paid 85baht for my meal. Overall, I would definitely highly recommend if you are in the asok area. || Fried rice with pork is my most favourite dish in bangkok so far - very tasty and fragrant. The stir-fried kee mow (flat noodles) with basil was also good. Felt that the basil pork and garlic-pepper pork was alright. Portions are not very big but it's very affordable! || A true hidden gem  Super non-descript and unassuming - don't be fooled  The pad kra pow packs flavour and is just the right portion. Absolutely loved the no frills no thrills experience here - just an elderly couple serving up a good plate. || Basil pork rice was average, but definitely try the pork fried rice and pad kee mao! Very affordable and authentic. However, location is about a 10 minute walk from Asok BTS station and food took a while to serve. || Found this hidden gem in a blog and decided to give it a go since I’m staying in the area.  Was not disappointed as it was a local shop that sells limited food choices but of awesome taste. There were multiple locals queuing and having lunch while we were having our meals in the shop itself, proving itself to be renowned locally as well.  2 plates of stir fried pork and minced pork rice with omelette costs 150 baht, pretty good value for money!  Will definitely return if I’m in the area looking for a quick bite! || Wok hei! Was here at around 11am, wasn’t crowded so ordered a pork basil rice and fried kway teow, one of the best pork basil rice I’ve ever had in Bangkok, the kway teow is full of wok hei, simple yet delicious.. service is quick and have a English menu. Will definitely be back! || Mark Wiens recommended this place.  I personally thought that the portioning of minced pork was a bit too little to the rice. Flavour wise it wasn’t so strong as well. Nonetheless the wok hei taste was present. Generally above average but not the best pad krapow || We came across this little spot on a food blog and it looked delicious. We went there and it did not disappoint. My husband had the stir fried pork over rice with a fried egg (extra cost-10 baht) and I had the stir fried noodles with pork and a fried egg. The noodles are meant to be spicy but I wasn’t sure how spicy it would be and not willing to risk it, I asked if they could make it less spicy and it was not a problem. I highly recommend it.

so many food stalls to mesmerize me, food lovers' paradise, actually along the long walk there are also lots of eateries, cafe, dessert houses and fast food chain restaurant like mcdonald or kfc, but unless in a hurry, one would be tempted by the fantastic array of good looking foods, dishes and fruits on display by the street food  stalls, especially on A good sunny day, good to taste Thai delicacy under gentle warm sunlight with soft light breeze on the street

Absolutely LOVED it here! I can't believe that the museum is free to the public! Very few people were there when I went on a Saturday afternoon. The displays were informative, and did a wonderful job of telling a cohesive story about how … || Absolutely wonderful experience in this hidden gem. Lots of interactive displays and the docents were really helpful in answering a range of questions. All exhibits are bilingually labelled and they go the extra mile to explain why the … || The museum is located inside the Learning Center of the Bank of Thailand. Museum has 12:00-13:00 lunch brake. … || Admission is free. Tight security. They will scan your belongings. After the check, register yourself at the museum counter. The guide will bring you to the tour. The tour starts at the bottom of the room, which is 6 meter below the ground. … || Went here when it was quiet, got warmly welcomed by the well spoken staff. Absolutely fantastic tour, way more in depth than I expected! Lots of history and well preserved building in amazing location. Definitely recommended for people interested in economics and numismatics. || Well-decorated free-entry library with great facilities. Can be here to get there. Good place for reading books or get some work done. Plenty of space tp settle, just look for the corner you prefer. I recommend this place personally if … || You can see the history of money in Thailand and enjoy the river views around the hangover bridge. Various notes and printing machines and alternative exchange materials. After touring, you can drink chill and nice drink in the coffee shop. || Nice building with a modern museum and Library. Coming at sunset is recommended, as the terrace affords lovely views of the river. I came during the Bangkok Art Biennial and there were some special exhibitions as well as the standard displays. || Really nice place. Museum was possible the best in Thailand, good information, interestingly presented, great English, interactive, related to wider history. For such a potentially boring topic it was a revelation. Also free parking, beautiful views. Even if you have no interest in the topic, worth a visit || Nice space for visiting and learning. The building is well designed. Inside is library, co-working space and museum. Outside is a view from Chaopraya river and Rama 8 bridge.

You need to buy the ticket at another museum building nearby (the Siriraj Medical Museum). It’s only THB 80 and covers entry to both museums, so it’s a pretty good deal.  The Congdon Anatomical Museum itself is on the 3rd floor with no elevator, and there’s no air conditioning, so be prepared — it can get a bit warm. The place feels a little old and tired, but it’s actually really well organized and has some fascinating displays. Definitely worth a quick visit if you’re already checking out the Medical Museum! || Worth visiting, make sure you come before 4.30 p.m. || This museum is in vicinity of Siriraj Medical Museum, hospital, and medical faculty. This area is big and signage can be confusing. There are 7 museums but only available access to 5 museums. Congdon Anatomical Museum is open and is situated near Sri Savarindira building. Please check online for map area. || As a pregnant woman, I am not sure why I chose to spend my morning in Bangkok looking at dead babies in formaldehyde...but, here I am!! The numbers of bodies and specimens can be overwhelming, so it is not for the faint hearted. Some parents brought their children, which I found an odd choice. If you are interested in human anatomy and science and have a morbid curiosity for the dead, then, this is your place! || Very interesting. Could have been more signs in English. || Was very interesting. You buy tickets to multiple museums and all were worth checking out. Maybe 3 or 4 hours to go slowly through it all. Finding the other museums was a little confusing || The Congdon Anatomical Museum, located in Bangkok, is a fascinating and educational destination dedicated to the study of human anatomy. This museum is renowned for its extensive collection of anatomical specimens and medical artifacts, offering visitors a unique and in-depth look at the complexities of the human body.  Educational Value: One of the main attractions of the Congdon Anatomical Museum is its impressive collection of anatomical models, preserved specimens, and medical instruments. The museum’s exhibits provide detailed insights into human anatomy and physiology, making it an invaluable resource for students, medical professionals, and anyone interested in the science of the human body. The displays cover various aspects of anatomy, including skeletal structures, organ systems, and developmental stages.  Historical Significance: The museum is named after Dr. Congdon, a prominent figure in the field of anatomy, whose contributions to medical science are celebrated through this collection. The historical context of the museum adds depth to the visitor experience, as it highlights the evolution of anatomical study and medical practice over time.  Exhibits and Collections: The Congdon Anatomical Museum features a range of exhibits that showcase detailed anatomical models and preserved specimens. These displays are meticulously curated to provide accurate and informative representations of human anatomy. The museum also includes historical medical instruments and educational materials that illustrate the progress of anatomical research and medical technology.  Visitor Experience: The museum offers a quiet and focused environment that encourages learning and exploration. The exhibits are well-organized, with clear labels and informative descriptions that enhance the educational experience. The staff are knowledgeable and can provide additional information or answer questions about the exhibits and their significance.  Accessibility and Environment: The museum is designed to be accessible to visitors, with thoughtful arrangements to facilitate an engaging experience. The atmosphere is respectful and contemplative, reflecting the seriousness of the subject matter while providing a valuable learning opportunity.  Overall Impression: The Congdon Anatomical Museum is a unique and enriching destination for those interested in human anatomy and medical science. Its extensive collection, educational focus, and historical context make it a valuable resource for learning about the human body and the history of anatomical study. Whether you're a student, a medical professional, or simply curious about the intricacies of human anatomy, the museum offers a comprehensive and insightful experience. || Pretty confronting museum with preserved babies and body parts but also interesting displays such as a complete nervous system and lymphatic system. Worth checking out for an hour or so. || Definitely a place for the inquisitive. All the exhibitions were displayed nicely but all the information was in Thai only. We had a good understanding of what we were looking at,but can be some what confusing for some. You are also not allowed to take any photos. || Affordable and interesting site I arrived via river boat and came via a small local market That's worth poking around. Museum itself was rather grousome at times and did feel exploitive Not much in English which creeped me out more when looking at crime scenes or medical oddities I only took the two museum option Some stairs to climb and the second one no air con

place_name: Local Museum of Bangkok - Bangkok Noi
reviews_content: Small (one room) but interesting museum about the history of the Bangkok Noi area with some artifacts, photographs, and explanations in both Thai and English. Worth a while if you are in the neighborhood. It's located inside a school so a bit hard to find. You have to enter the school campus via the entrance on Soi Charan Sanitwong 32 and then the museum is directly on the left. Staff is very friendly and keen to help. || A bit hard to find (it’s tucked into a building inside the temple school grounds), but well worth a visit if you’re in the area and curious about the history of Old Thonburi and Bangkok Noi. Staff are very friendly and helpful, though you’ll need a translation app if you don’t speak Thai. || The area is interesting. The exhibits and arrangement of the items can be made more interesting. The staff are informative and willing. If there is lighting and presentation, along with regular activities, it will make more people know about it. And emphasize that people in the community know about the history of the area. The community is very interesting. Add other things to attract people. It will respond to the trend of walking in the community at once. || Bangkok Local Museum, Bangkok Noi District..located within the grounds of Wat Suwannaram Witthayakhom School. It is a small museum. || The speakers were very cooperative and provided excellent information. || It is a good local museum. || A very nice place to visit.

This museum was an incredible experience. I loved the top floor that had the queen‘s actual outfits throughout the years, with information about the designers. But the first floor area with timeline information was incredible. Make sure you visit the first floor area and don’t just go up the stairs, you won’t regret it. The picture of the timeline I have is only the very first panel. || A very pleasant way to spend 1/2 day in Bangkok.  The grounds and buildings depict Thailand as it was in the 19th  and early 20th centuries - well before air conditioning.  Admission is restricted, call before visiting. || Always closed seems permanent from the policeman I asked || It’s closed for a while without knowing when it’s going to reopen. || Tried to visit today, but not possible to enter the site.

I HAD A GREAT EXPERIENCE AS I VISITED THE MUSEUM HERE, IT WAS VERY IMPRESSIVE. AND THERE HAS VERY ATRACTIVE DISPLAY WITH GOOD VIBES AND GOOD LIGHTING,TOO || Nice place to take a look when visit Bangkok. Great experience. Highly recommended. || Well arrange and organized || Thank you for sharing with me and the world. || Awesome museum in Bangkok
Brother Niphon's service is very, very good.

The view from Mahanakhon SkyWalk is absolutely stunning! If you dine at Ojo restaurant and spend at least 2,500 THB per person, you can go up to the SkyWalk for free 🌇  The panorama is breathtaking — you can clearly see the Chao Phraya River and IconSiam, especially beautiful during sunset. 💫 There’s also a laser room and a cartoon-themed area inside. The regular entrance ticket costs around 350 THB. || Well worth a visit, unless perhaps you suffer vertigo? We visited at around noon on a Wednesday and the experience was faultless. Guessing much depends on the weather, especially wind conditions, rain or smog, but hour we spent there it was overcast but beautiful. It’s also worth paying extra (350B) for the light show exhibition. Over 60? Bring proof - a phone pic of your passport will do - and you’ll receive a generous discount. Recommended. || A magnificent building. Great views and lots to experience. The price is reasonable and you can get by here without a guide. The staff welcomes you warmly and provides great guidance. || Mahanakhon Square is a vibrant hub in Bangkok, home to the iconic King Power Mahanakhon skyscraper. This mixed-use development offers a blend of high-end retail, dining, and entertainment. Explore the upscale shops, indulge in delicious cuisine at various restaurants, or catch a movie at the cinema. The square also hosts events and exhibitions, adding to its dynamic atmosphere. With its convenient location and diverse offerings, Mahanakhon Square is a must-visit destination for both locals and tourists seeking a taste of modern Bangkok. || Too crowded don’t expect to take good photos as it’s over crowded during peak hours. Pre book is preferred || Must visit area if you’re in Bangkok. Here you’ll find King Power Mahanakhon skywalk and i-tilt attractions at the top of the unique tower. || Lots of space for people to evacuate during Bangkok earthquake. || Nice entertainment center with awesome views. || Incredible views of Bangkok, fun glass walkway, pricy but worth the visit || Fantastic experience, recommend the tilt experience as well.  Weekday was really good with very little crowd and seamless experience.

I recently explored the magnificent Icon Siam 🤩, a true Bangkok signature. The architecture is stunning, blending traditional Thai elements with modern design; I found myself captivated. Inside, I discovered a diverse range of shops, from luxury brands to local crafts. Moreover, I savored delicious Thai cuisine while enjoying the Chao Phraya River view 🏞️. Icon Siam perfectly encapsulates Bangkok's vibrant spirit, making it a must-visit destination. || I've visited ICONSIAM park a few times now- sometimes just on the way out of the mall, and recently to board a dinner cruise. Each time, there has been some kind of family-friendly installment or event on. We were glad to catch the light show on our last visit! || Visited in June 2025. It is a small park in ICONSIAM shopping mall which can be easily accessed through Apple Store also. The river and city view from the park is really amazing. || While IconSiam is worth a visit to look at the river views from the top and see the waterfall, its not somewhere to shop. I was expecting to pick up some bargains here, but the things I was looking at were significantly cheaper in London. Its not somewhere to go for shopping, its ridiculously expensive. I would recommend going to the bar on the top floor for the views over the river, especially at night and its an easy stop on the tourist boat. || Modern and one of the most crowded mall in Bangkok. I went there by public boat, it was a unique experience.  Inside there was a "man-made floating market" Around 6-7pm, I get to see water show in front of the mall, pretty good show.. || Awesome place! The water show was beautiful. Be careful it will splash you if your too close😁 || I went during the weekday and around 5 and 6. I went to eat at the restaurant to see the sunset and enjoy a nice dinner. It's beautiful to take pictures a videos. This mall is huge,  there are a lot of floors and also a tall waterfall.  It's beautiful when it lights up, it's right next to a couple of restaurants.  You can choose to eat inside or outside. You can easily spend a couple of hours here. || ICONSIAM Park is an absolute delight and a must-visit destination in Bangkok! The sprawling riverside location along the Chao Phraya River offers a perfect blend of nature, culture, and modernity. The beautifully landscaped gardens and serene water features provide a refreshing escape from the city bustle, while the iconic Siam Paragon Ferris Wheel offers stunning panoramic views of the river and skyline. The park’s integration with the ICONSIAM shopping complex makes it convenient to enjoy world-class shopping and dining afterward, with a variety of delicious Thai and international cuisine options. The clean pathways, well-maintained facilities, and friendly staff create a welcoming atmosphere for families, couples, and solo travelers alike. I especially loved the vibrant cultural events and light displays that add a magical touch in the evenings. Highly recommend this gem for a relaxing and memorable day out! || It's a must go place if you're in Bangkok and nearby areas. From Observation Deck you can enjoy the most famous musical fountain show i.e. the longest fountain show in South East Asia, you will hear the least music sound but you can make lovely videos of the show from the observation deck which is much better than the ground floor. Also it's a selfie and photo livers deck as electrical LED poles are Wow and River view from there is also Wow! || One of the most beautiful malls in Asean. The ground floor lobby has a man made floating market with a thriving market for street food and local handicrafts. Multi luxury brands and other segments. What I'm impressed with is the attention to details in the ceiling, layout and ID, including the choice of materials and lighting. The architect must've spent a lot of effort on this project.

We went to the observation deck as part of our dinner buffet experience but you can go to the deck as it's own standalone experience. The deck is an internal area protected from the elements and has great 360° views of Bangkok. The views are amazing during daylight hours but at sunset or at nighttime they are stunning. There are several areas for your Instagram photos so swings, a balloon basket and even a Tuktuk allow you to pose to your hearts delight. A very good place to visit whilst you are in Bangkok and I would recommend combining it with the buffet experience as well which was excellent. || I got an affordable rate on Agoda to stay here, and you have free access to the observation deck during your stay. I went up to the revolving open-air rooftop several times; there is a nice breeze at night and the view reminds me of New York City in some way. It's really pretty to see, but I do wonder, behind the glitz of the city lights, you can still think of the many pockets and swaths of poverty in the midst of it. Very pretty, but it makes you wonder, who are all these pretty lights built for? All in all though, it's probably one of the best city views I've seen from an observatory, because it's tall and expansive, and because several of Bangkok's buildings have character, and because there's a 360 degree view on a revolving platform, and there's a nice breeze most days. I think it can do better with seats for people though! || A great spot to enjoy city views and take amazing photos. For 450 baht, the ticket includes: •	Floor 77: observation deck •	Floor 83: one free drink •	Floor 84: rotating observation deck with a fantastic atmosphere  Just relax and enjoy your time. || Visiting the observation deck at the Baiyoke Sky Tower was one of the highlights of my trip to Bangkok. The experience begins with a swift elevator ride up to the 77th floor, where the indoor viewing area offers a sweeping 360-degree panorama of the sprawling city — a perfect place to take in the skyline, spot landmarks, and watch life unfold far below.  What makes this attraction particularly special is the rotating sky deck on the 84th floor. Here you can steadily walk around as the platform gently turns, giving you uninterrupted views of Bangkok in every direction without needing to move yourself.  The city looks magical at sunset or when lit up at night — truly a photographer’s dream and an unforgettable way to appreciate the scale and energy of this vibrant metropolis.  The ticket price is reasonable for what you get, and often includes a complimentary drink, which adds nice value to the experience.  While sections of the observatory and surrounding facilities feel a bit dated, that doesn’t detract much from the breathtaking views you’re there for. All in all, it’s well worth a visit if you’re curious to see Bangkok from above. || It is not the tallest building in Bangkok, nor the most beautiful. But the view from the top is beautiful and worth visiting. I liked the idea of the rotating platform on the 84th floor, it is something unique and useful for the tired or lazy. There is also a bar on the 83rd floor, a bit outdated. The entrance ticket also includes a drink. Quite a lot of fingerprints on the windows, they should be cleaned more often. || Here’s another must do in Bangkok! The view, the bar, the buffet 3 different ones to choose between and once again; the VIEW! Wow! Don’t miss this and for the money, it’s top value and great selection of tasty food (wee Dunedin the Crystal restaurant), super location also downstairs for the street markets and vibes! Gotta give it a go! || The view is nice especially when night time. It is so relaxing and astonishing watching the whole 360 degree view from the top. The foods are also nice and you have a lot of choices. It might not be that tasty but it is already fine to enjoy your savor. || Quite run down, but has a lot of charm. One of the tallest buildings in Thailand that you can go to the top of for only 500 Baht. The price includes a 20-minute foot and calf massage. The revolving deck is outdoors. I recommend taking the stairs down from the top deck to the bottom deck to see the crazy outer space mural that spans 20 floors of the staircase. || One of the best views of Bangkok. Can go to observation deck if you stay at the hotel (Baiyoke Sky) or buy a drink at the bar. The evening and night offers great views || Bangkok has a few viewing towers and perhaps this is one of the more affordable ones, roughly 12 euros 66.  You also get a complimentary drink as part of your purchase which is good.  Not so busy too - so time to relax and take it all in . Views are pretty good, although Bangkok looked slightly smoggy the day we were there.  The rotating tower is ok, takes a bit of getting used to it, but worth a walk around.  All in all - worth a try out and spent an enjoyable few hours here.

Chitholes, I’ve known a few, but none as good as this Chithole.  Hands down, this Chithole located on the side of the Chaophraya River, and at … || Good vibes, amazing view by the river ☁️ Like the Thai craft beer 🍺 support the local. … || Nice evening for tasty beers on the Chao Praya River.  Located in the Royal River Hotel. Tasted 6 out of 18 beers on tap.  Black lager, NEIPA, Kolsch, Red IPA, DIPA, and Porter - all yummy.   Already planning to go back and try some more, since it’s within stumbling distance. || Accessed by entering the The Royal river hotel and heading towards the river. They have a good selection of craft beer and the staff are helpful to recommend. A little bit expensive, but probably about the standard price you pay for craft … || Craft beer with good view || Nice place but it was totally empty the night we were there. Food nice but nothing special and small portions. Beer very nice though. || This place is suitable for local craft beers lover They have many craft beers on tap and price is so cheap Drinking with good vibe by the chaopaya river and you can order food from royal rover hotel || Just Stopped In For A Beer And Cocktail. Great Selection Of Beers || New CHIT branch on Charan rd and riverside with great view.There are  a ot of craft beer for chosen and a food from the hotel. Resonable beer price! || An excellent riverside craft beer bar in Bangkok.  With optional food choices from other restaurants at the hotel served at your table. …

✨A Chilling Riverside Bar You’ll Instantly Fall in Love With✨  If you’re looking for a spot to reset your mood on a lazy afternoon, this riverside bar is exactly where you need to be. A cozy little place right by the water, with a light breeze drifting through—just sitting down already feels refreshing.  The prices are friendly, the service is genuinely good, and the food turns out surprisingly delicious. Drinks come in both refreshing and easy-sipping options, perfect for relaxing while watching the river flow by.  The best time to visit? Late afternoon, when the sunlight softens and the riverside breeze kicks in. It’s the ultimate chillax vibe, where you can sit for hours, enjoy good music, good food, and let time move as slowly as you want.  If you’re searching for a place to chat, unwind, sip, and soak in a beautiful river view—this is the spot. 😉✨ || Definitely worth the visit. Right on the water, decent little menu, great priced beers and rum, and it attracts the most interesting and engaging people! They do have out by times so make sure to respect their reservations  but it is definitely a great place to visit! || Lovely to find a river view spot with reasonable prices and have a decent glass of wine. They serve food which looks pretty good too, willing to try next time. Love view in the evening with all the night lights, service is spot on, very quick. Love it || Open-air bar beside the Chao Phraya River near the Shangri-La. Frequented by expats, it offers cold beer, river views, and constant boat traffic. The grilled chicken was well-cooked and paired perfectly with a large Leo. I’ll return to try the Pad Thai on my next visit. || What a great local riverside bar. Great owner! Best Thai food I’ve had in the 3 weeks I was in Thailand. Incredible views. Right on the water!! Can’t wait to come back to Bangkok just for the beer,Tom Yum and friendly conversation. || This is the place. If you had to describe Bangkok in a restaurant - THIS IS THE PLACE.  A bit manic, a bit disjointed, a bit mis-matched in furnishings - therefore this place was perfect.  Staff were amazing, food was amazing and beer was ice cold. What more do you need from a Thai Restaurant in Bangkok?  If you're luckily enough to get a river view seat - it adds to the charm this place has.  If you're a snob and like fine dining - go elsewhere. If you want one of the best food experiences in Bangkok - come here.  Only thing I'd say is when we visited a second time, the restaurant was closed at 11:20 saying it was open until 00:00. The first experience was so good - that I couldn't marl them down for this. I highly recommend jack's bar. Make sure you order the Laab Moo Tod. || Hidden gem. Great prices. Weekdays daytime has plenty of seats. Busier otherwise. Reservation for dinner is highly recommended.  Pro-tip, water transport is easy. They have a  small dock so you can be picked up by your water taxi. They can get you a water taxi also. || One of my favorite spots in Bangkok right next to the Shangri-La with stunning views of the river and boats passing by and a large beer for 120 baht. Can’t beat the view and feels like some carribean shack. They have own pier with long boats to rent out. || A cool place with a beautiful atmosphere. Sipping your beer or wine with an astonishing view on the Chao Phraya. The staff is very friendly and helpful. It’s not only a bar, you can also get food which is very delicious at moderate prices. To be sure getting a seat, come around before, to have a reservation done. Will always come back to here! || Super fun experience at Jacks Bar! Drinks are cheap and the food is tasty, fresh, with many options. This place seems to fill up quick, so get there early if you want one of the coveted spots literately right next to the river. Although our table seat still lets you see the action on the river. Nothing fancy here, so no need to dress up.

It was just perfect Bangkok greeting from the first evening here. Staff is super friendly, food was delicious and not expensive. Also, you can watch street life happening just by having a beer. || Amazing in every way! We are so happy we stumbled across this restaurant. Everything from food to atmosphere and service was fabulous! They make the food fresh to order and even perfectly catered to us as vegans. Ir truly IS Cheaper & Better street food. GO HERE! || I think this place is exactly what it says it is, it’s cheap and it’s good food. We had the Pad Si Ew, the chicken fried rice, and the fried chicken stir fry dish. All were good dishes and total was 230 baht including a bottle of water.  Updated Edit - we went back here the following night and ordered a four items - shrimp fried rice, chicken pad si ew, spring rolls, and fried chicken stir fry - that all totaled to 300 baht. Definitely recommend! || Had the pleasure of eating here and was pleasantly surprised by the quality and flavor of the food. I’m a big fan of spicy dishes, and I loved that they offer special spicy sauces you can add to your meal.  I tried the Pad Thai, mango sticky rice, Tom Yum, fried gyozas, papaya salad, and grilled squid, everything was fresh and delicious. The fresh coconuts were a nice touch, and I appreciated that they can pack the mango sticky rice to go.  On top of the amazing food, the staff are so nice and caring, which made the whole experience even better. I’m definitely looking forward to coming back! || We were so hungry after our trip and so we stopped by due to many good reviews. Overall it was an interesting experience. Would we go back?  Likely not, but overall it was an interesting experience. The food choices were abundance. We ordered pad kra pao, pad thai, sukiyaki, and fresh coconut. The best part was the coconut. It was refreshing. The food taste did not meet our expectations. To set the expectations straight, we are Lao, and so our taste expectations were rather high. With that said, the food we had were a disappointment. The taste did not meet our expectations at all. It tasted rather bland and the pad kra pao was lacking the holy basil (kao pao). The prices were fair based on the restaurant’s name. We spent 300 baht for the 3 dishes and coconut. The environment was interesting. The restaurant is on the sidewalk. Cars and motorcycles were whizzing close by as we sat and watch and ate. Even though it was a one way street, that is a mere suggestion because they were traveling in both directions. It was a good experience and one to remember. || Should give Michelin Star this tiny street restaurant! The owner is friendly, attentive and give a good suggestion for catch of the day. We ordered 5 big shrimps, only 200 Thai Bat, so cheap but so good! Highly recommended! || Ordered their Grilled Prawns which was fresh and huge. Chilli crab was delicious gravy but crab is small flower crab. Tom Yum soup was decent, and cabbage just huge serving.  Their prices are super reasonable,  especially for the grilled prawns.  Staff are very friendly. They can speak some English and Chinese.  They have 2 shops, at the market and opposite the mosque which is air-conditioned and more comfortable. Worth coming back. || It really is cheaper and better. I got 4 dishes, they were good and really cheap. The owner or manager or whoever was really nice absolutely fantastic service. Would definitely recommend it. || Visited CHEAPER AND BETTER and guess what?? this place lives up to its name! I had the tom yum soup, and it was hands down the best I’ve ever had. Portions are generous, the staff is super friendly, and the prices are four times cheaper than at the hotel. Definitely a must-try, for (1) food and (2) the vibe! || Liked the place so much we went to eat 3 times during our stay in Bangkok.  Food is good and price is good.  Very friendly staff.  Highly recommended.

Local small food court for mostly locals working in the area. Had the pork offal dark soup. Very tasty and affordable. Vendor speaks a bit of English so its great for my orders with extra tofu and no noodles. Cost me 90 baht. Delicious || I love this place. It's mostly Thai people grabbing breakfast on the way to work. There are several stalls with different choices. The menus are in Thai, but the vendors speak enough English to get by, and you can always use Google translate.  The food is outstanding. Everyone is very friendly. If you enjoy a more local experience I think you'll like it. If you haven't tried stepping out of the tourist zone, this is a great place to start. 😊 || A small food hall with delicious home cooked Thai food. Many different options of food. We tried the Chinese noodles as well as rice plate with curry, fried fish, fried chicken, and vegetables. All were fresh and excellent. There is even a drink stand where you can buy Thai tea, chrysanthemum tea, and Thai coffee. Extremely affordable as well. 50-100 baht per dish. There are fans so there are minimal bugs however there is no AC so can be a little hot and humid inside. Still worth the visit. || This place open its shutters at 4am for food prep and start serving only after 5 ish. There are 6 individual stalls, one selling drinks. For tourists its best to come for breakfast or brunch as the office workers start pouring in around 11am- 1.30pm it can get super crowded. By 2pm the stall selling different main & side courses to go with rice have not much left. We had the Kway Chap which is the Pork meat & offals with rice noodles, really tasty. But if business is good that day, there isn’t much left so no point going after 2pm. Food is as local as you can get, tasty and cheap. || Really delicious, affordable, authentic local food! I got my rice with 3 side dishes (green curry, spicy pork salad, and deep fried chicken with kale) for 60 baht. Recommend this place!!! || These are series of stalls. I tried the one in the middle by the entrance that serves vegetarian food. The rice with bamboo shots and bok choy was delicious and super fresh, Highly recommended. || Large selection of traditional Thai food. Fresh and tasty food with super friendly service. Had green curry and pad krapow. Both were excellent. Most dishes are 30-40 Baht. || Typical Thai food for the locals at local prices. If u wish to experience how the Thai eat daily this is the place to go in downtown Sukhumvit. Communication is not a problem as all the hawkers speak basic English. Hygiene is acceptable. || Overall the place is clean and people are nice. The food is fresh and quite few options to choose from. The drinks are sold at the shop in the back. English is not used here but menus are available in English. || Best Chinese noodle soup 50 Bhat. We were the only westerners having lunch , that’s when you know you’ve found a good spot to eat  Highly recommend stopping here for lunch before continuing on to shopping at Terminal 21

Walked into this street not knowing what to expect and immediately got distracted by food on both sides. I told myself I would just grab one thing, then ended up stopping multiple times because everything smelled too good to ignore. It felt very local, busy without being overwhelming, and the food came out fast. By the time I left, I was full, slightly sweaty, and very satisfied. One of those streets where you do not plan a meal, you just let it happen. || Went there at 6 pm and many seller already there. Didnt buy things there but several seller sell their omelete rice & rice box for 25-30 baht. || Many choices and variety of local thai street food with cheap price. But sadly, the cleanliness is poor. You can easily spot rats everywhere. || Make sure to stop at this lady’s place, the best pork I’ve had in my life. || Quite local. Very much of the same thing in terms of local food. There are side alleys to explore as well. Try the Soi across the road as well. Soi Phetchaburi 10. Same same but different. Worth a looksie if have t done it yet. I went stall by stall peeked at what’s cookn with the usual sawadee krap ... and graze away... some are actual homes that the family has just started cooking out front to sell. || I had the pork leg rice by a lady within a street . Price food and service

place_name: Myth I Bangkok Street food | Best mango sticky rice

reviews_content: No trip to Bangkok is complete unless you eat the street food and some of my favorites can be found here. You'd need a prodigious appetite and a capacity to match if your intention is to try half of the stalls in one sitting, so it would be a good idea to visit over a couple of meals ( or even a couple of days if you intend to include Silom's back alley sois nearby which are also lined with street stalls during lunch ).  One of my favorite stalls is the fried dumplings that come with several choices of filling. Similar to the Teochew soon kway (which is normally steamed), this glutinous dumpling is instead fried in a shallow pan of oil to a crisp and served with a sweet black soy sauce. My favorite fillings are either the steamed chives or bamboo shoots. Great as a starter as you make your way down the street to try the heavier stuff (all of which are thankfully light on the wallet) ! || Tried Tokyo and coconut cake here, tokyos soft and blend, not crispy, coconut cakes not delicious as well, maybe try other food next time. || Tried omelette rice where you can choose your ingredients and chicken wings, the chili sauce is so special. Other food too. || So many delicious foods on offer. Recommend the banana coconut pancake. || Restaurant Yellorice. We had a very good and unforgetable experience. Very good food, great service and honest price! || This fried banana shop is good … very crispy and tasty 👍 30 baht per set || Great chicken and rice meal (80 baht, extra large) beside a busy road. || Not very long street stalk about 15 stalls, || A lot of delicious food on this street from morning till night || Papaya Chicken salad must try!

reviews_content: I loved this place! The people were very friendly, the food tasted awesome and a nice cute little setup! Chef Goji and I go some time back. I've known him ever since he first arrived in BKK and lit up the scene more than 7 years back.  As Chef Goji discovered to his delight, I do not live in BKK. No work trip to BKK would be complete without a visit. And I make trips up just to dine with him. The latest was the weekend of 26-27 September 2025. Dinner and then lunch the next day before I flew home. Hedonistic perhaps but SO worth the visit!  Dining with Chef Goji is not just about good food. He is trusted and I just leave myself in his good hands. And he is a great conversationalist. So dedicated to his craft and ceaselessly passionate.  Hence, it is always a joy to drop by!  [Updated 9 Nov 2025 with new photos from visit for dinner on 7 Nov 2025 and lunch on 8 Nov 2025]  Just came back from another lightning visit to Bangkok to sample the autumn seasonal offerings from Chef Goji. The food was exquisite as always and Chef Goji was great as ever.  He was just a little concerned as to whether I would make my 3.50 pm flight home. Very kind of him. I travel light and only have a backpack. I have my boarding pass and I am able to use the priority lane at the airport.  The highlight of this visit has to the female snow crab. “Glorified Hibachi”  My wife said it perfectly.  We’re not critically acclaimed chefs or have any culinary background, but don’t understand how this can be rated the number 1 restaurant in Asia. For the price you pay ($500 USD), yes you get wine pairing and it includes the gratuity (the staff deserves it), but we expected tastier food. The food is “avant garde”, yes, provocative, yes, but after every bite, you just take a step back and think of how tasty any food stall must be outside since you’re in Bangkok. It’s okay if the chef and team don’t care, but when you spend a thousand for a couple in a city like Thailand, as a guest, it’s perfectly ok to care.  The service of the staff and the narration by the head chef is great. It feels a little condescending at times to be told what is so interesting about the dish - like of course the dish is interesting - that’s why we’re here. A painter or musician doesn’t tell you WHY their art is great — it just lands or it doesn’t.  Beyond that, some parts of the menu were innovative in the sense that the bite didn’t look like what it was supposed to taste like but it lacked a cohesive menu. The journey through three countries didn’t land as well as they should have - why did we pick those countries, what do the dishes have in common? The whole night was an unfinished story with no real plot except that Gaggan and team thought these dishes should be presented a certain way.  The music is uncomfortably loud (with some odd choices) and the wine pairing feels light for how much you’re paying - maybe two full glasses at best.  I think this is an easy skip in Bangkok. There are innovative restaurants popping up on the scene and you can honestly get a tastier and memorable meal on the street for 10X less. || One of the most unforgettable dining experiences I’ve ever had! The atmosphere at Gaggan is fun, lively, and completely unpretentious  part dinner, part performance, and a little bit of art. The food was absolutely insane in the best possible way: clever, playful, and delicious…Every course surprised us, and the whole night felt like a culinary show. I laughed, danced a little, and savored every bite. Easily the best meal I’ve had in Bangkok I can’t recommend it enough! || For the first time a meal that numbed me!!! I tried so hard to put my Gaggan experience into words… but my fingers refused to move. How do you describe something that goes beyond food? Was it the flavours? Was it the music? The energy in the room? The team that moved like one heartbeat? Or was it the magician himself—the biggest showman the culinary world has ever seen? Those three hours were pure theatre. A jaw-dropping, mind-bending, heart-thumping journey. If you truly want to experience Gaggan, you must go to Bangkok. Only then can you feel the warmth, the madness, the passion that his entire team pours into every moment. It’s rare to see a brigade so perfectly in sync with a chef’s vision. The wine pairings were exceptional, and Vladimir guiding us through each pour was like icing on an already unforgettable cake. As Gaggan calls it, “cooksicle” and “curry ok kay”, I feel blessed, humbled and privileged to have seen him perform right in front of my eyes. This is not just Indian, not just Japanese, not just Thai. It is Gaggan, A category of its own!!! || aggan blew us away. Surprising, bold flavors, incredibly fun service, and pacing that’s beyond perfect. I’ve never experienced a 24-course menu with this level of precision and we’ve eaten at top restaurants across the globe. Each course felt like a performance, each bite a surprise, and the energy of the team made the night unforgettable. It’s not just dinner, it’s an experience. || If dining at Valhalla is described as magical and wonderful, then Gaggan’s truly is Valhalla. It isn’t just dining — it’s singing, interacting, laughing… it’s a full celebration.  This is not your typical fine-dining evening. It’s an experience. If you’re hoping to sit and talk business or have a long personal chat, Chef Gaggan simply won’t let you — in the best possible way.  The reservation process was surprisingly simple: a WhatsApp message and a payment link. A few hours later, I found myself stepping into the mind of Chef Gaggan. The space is draped in hanging vines, illuminated by a giant neon caricature of the man himself with the words “Be a Rebel.” Everywhere you look, there’s a playful touch waiting to be noticed. Our host was warm and welcoming, guiding me to my seat. With only 14 guests, it feels more like a theatre than a restaurant. What impressed me most was how every staff member addressed me by name — that level of personal attention speaks volumes.  Chef Gaggan personally greets each guest and sets the tone with a heartfelt welcome speech. What followed was a 25-course journey blending flavours from India, Thailand, and Japan. From the signature Yogurt Explosion with crackling candy, to the silky brain mousse, to the festive chaos of Gulal, and finally the comforting simplicity of rice and fish — every course had a story, a purpose, and a little bit of rebellion.  Their philosophy of sourcing the best ingredients from around the world and letting them shine truly comes through. The price also includes wine or mocktail pairing, and the sommelier was exceptional — knowledgeable, enthusiastic, and spot-on with every pairing. Some of the wines were genuinely among the best I’ve ever had.  This is an experience worth having. If you’re visiting Bangkok, I’d highly recommend booking a seat. It is on the pricier side, but considering the wine pairing and the three-hour culinary performance you’re getting, it feels balanced and absolutely worthwhile.  Chef Gaggan and team — keep the magic alive.  From Meals I Love Forever (MILF) || 25 unique dishes presented during a show/lecture that is like nothing I never experienced before. So many interesting combinations of flavours and textures in a totally different way. It’s brave to start something like this, and it’s not for everyone. Me personally loved it. I was here a few years ago and it’s even better today. They really nailed it. The combination of food and drinks, colours, textures and the music! I left happy, the team really gave everything here. || First time in Thailand – just two weeks. I wondered how to wrap up this trip, and eventually decided to book a seat for myself at Gaggan in Bangkok.  No wonder it’s ranked #1 in Asia and #6 in the world.  An out-of-body, multi-sensory experience—unapologetic and uncompromising. Step inside and everything else fades away— flawless wine pairing phenomenal music pairing dynamic lighting and of course, 25 unforgettable courses.  An absolutely insane way to end this trip. || Mixed thoughts on our visit here. The service and food is absolutely outstanding, no doubt. The team has put in a lot of thought into developing the menu in a very unique way, with a story behind each dish. The wine pairing was on the money for each dish. Loved the community style eating with Gaggan and the staff engaging with everyone during the meal. The only thing I found overwhelming was the music and clapping - it felt like a cheap Arabian Nights type show - that's not what I expected from this restaurant, which is supposed to be fine dining. That said, I understand that while Gaggan was preparing the last dish, the staff needed something to keep the diners engaged - but music and clapping? Just made it feel like a cheap theatric parlor trick. That said, Gaggan did say at the beginning of the meal that this was all about chaos - and that's exactly what this felt like! Overall a lovely dining experience, could've been better had it been less loud, and more controlled. But that's a personal preference. If you're visiting Bangkok, you kinda have to try to get a reservation here. Price tag is not that crazy considering how much you would pay for Michelin star restaurants in other parts of the world! || This is hands down the best food experience I’ve had in my entire life. I’ll be looking for more and better, but I’ll be hard pressed to find it. No wonder Gaggan made it to the #6 best in the world.  Amazing attentive and personalised service, awesome food journey across India, Japan and Thailand, and a multi-sensorial stimulus that makes the 25 courses a happy and cheerful walk in the park. || It’s not just a restaurant. It’s a show. Sometimes an uncomfortable one. Loud music, lots of directions and rules, lots of stories told, and great and creative food. Like the greatest hits from the 1980’s? You will be required to sing and clap along.

Truly amazing dinner at Sorn. Early courses highlight fresh seafood: river prawn with green mango, hand caught abalone with mangosteen, and crispy local fish scented with turmeric and curry paste. Raw and lightly cooked seafood as blue crab, lobster, and Babylon snail, moving fluidly between heat and freshness.  One of the most memorable dish is Crab Stick: the blue crab coated in chili paste and Mud Crab roe. Intensely spicy and deeply savory, it exemplifies the kitchen’s fearless approach to flavor. A fragrant coconut based soup follows, soothing the palate while maintaining depth and aroma.  The menu then pivots to vegetables and rice. A vibrant Southern Thai vegetable salad, mixed tableside, balances sweetness, crunch, and acidity. The Southern Jasmine rice cooked in a clay pot served with an array of condiments designed to amplify or tame the heat. It’s paired with some dishes: redtail catfish with stinky bean and Southern curry paste, Thai omelet crowned with tiger prawn, and morning glory enriched with abalone liver, dried scallop and shrimp. The sequence peaks with spicy beef, southern green curry and roti , before easing into a softer finish with plum soup.  End of the meal with dessert, as longan sorbet and jelly with sticky rice, offering a refreshing counterpoint to the earlier spicy courses. Meanwhile, the wine pairings are thoughtfully chosen to elevate the dining experience. Highly recommended! || One of the most impressive Asian restaurants I have ever been to!  Sorn is truly exceptional in preserving the authenticity of traditional Thai cuisine while adding a subtle touch of modern creativity in the presentation. Each dish is a masterpiece with beautiful plating and mouth-watering flavors that perfectly balance the essence of Thai taste.  The team takes great care in selecting high-quality local ingredients and blends them harmoniously from one dish to the next. Every bite showcases the diversity and depth of Thailand’s culinary heritage, elevated to a fine-dining level without losing its soul.  I honestly cannot find enough words to praise them. The best I can say is that if you are a food lover, you simply must experience Sorn for yourself. || From the moment you step into the intimate heritage house setting, the experience feels personal and intentional. Every detail from the warm service to the storytelling reflects Sorn’s mission to preserve, elevate and honor Southern Thai cuisine using ingredients sourced directly from small producers across the region.  Sorn is not just the best three Michelin starred restaurant in Thailand. It is a cultural landmark. A meal here is unforgettable, meaningful and genuinely world class. If you want to understand why Thai cuisine deserves its place at the very top of global gastronomy Sorn is essential. || It's good as it deserves the 3-star Michelin for the creativity, the use of premium ingredient, and the service. Most of the dishes are just probably too authentic, at least for me. Since it has pretty much the influence of southern Thai food, most of the dishes are extremely spicy. Request was made to drop the spicy level to the lowest possible, but still. Good rice though. It stands! || Sorn was a real disappointment.  From a food perspective, the dishes were good but ultimately not memorable. The flavours felt largely one-dimensional and, in my personal view, overly spicy to the point that it detracted from appreciating the nuances of the ingredients. Portion sizes were generous, but the sheer number of courses left us feeling uncomfortably full.  The greater let-down, however, was the service. It fell well short of what one would expect from a three Michelin star restaurant. Our waiter was inattentive throughout the evening — drinks were not topped up, the table was not cleaned between courses, and several dishes were removed before we had finished. There were also mistakes with our order and no apology for when they made an error. Furthermore, explanation of the dishes were flat and scripted without real knowledge of the dish when we asked further.  The most disappointing moment came at the end of the meal, when we were asked to wait outside the restaurant for our taxi because the restaurant was closing, despite it only being 10pm.  Overall, while the food was good, it lacked distinction, and the service was extremely poor. This is certainly not a restaurant worth making a special journey for, and I would recommend skipping it altogether. || Amazing Southern Thai Food  I’m Thai, but I was surprised to try so many new ingredients I’ve never had before. They picked us up from Sukhumvit 26 close to BTS and even gave us towels and shawls to stay dry and warm. Really thoughtful!  The price is totally worth it for a 3-star Michelin meal.  The only downside was that the table next to us was a bit loud, so it was a bit hard to hear the staff explain the dishes. But overall, it was an amazing experience. Highly recommended! || The food was excellent, but honestly I would expect more from a 3 starred.  In all fairness, everything was cooked to perfection and the taste was on point. The  Art Space Gallery offers an exceptional experience for art enthusiasts and casual visitors alike. As you step into the gallery, you are immediately captivated by the serene and welcoming atmosphere. The lighting is soft and perfectly highlights the stunning artworks on display, making the whole space feel both intimate and grand. Visitors are greeted with a warm smile by the staff, who are incredibly knowledgeable and eager to answer any questions about the exhibitions. The space is thoughtfully curated, with a mix of contemporary and classic pieces that inspire reflection and admiration.  What sets this gallery apart is the way it engages all your senses. The music played in the background is soothing, creating a calm ambiance that complements the visual experience. Visitors are invited to take their time, move at their own pace, and truly soak in each artwork without feeling rushed. Every corner of the gallery has been designed to encourage mindfulness and contemplation, making it a sanctuary for art lovers.  In addition to the stunning artworks, the gallery has a cozy café that offers a delightful range of food and beverages. The food is beautifully presented, and the flavors are just as artistic as the pieces on the walls. Their gourmet sandwiches, fresh salads, and artisanal pastries are made with locally sourced ingredients, ensuring freshness and taste. The café’s menu caters to all dietary preferences, from vegans to those with a sweet tooth.  Their beverage selection is equally impressive, featuring handpicked wines from local vineyards, specialty coffees, and refreshing herbal teas. Whether you’re a wine connoisseur or a casual tea drinker, the variety ensures there's something for everyone. The baristas and servers are attentive and skilled, always ready to offer suggestions based on your preferences.  The gallery often hosts interactive events such as artist talks, live painting sessions, and workshops that allow visitors to engage directly with the art and the artists. These events foster a sense of community, and the reactions from attendees are always enthusiastic and positive. People leave the gallery not only feeling inspired but also connected to a larger artistic community.  What really stands out is the gallery's dedication to creating an inclusive and inspiring environment. People from all walks of life are made to feel welcome, whether they are seasoned collectors or simply curious about art. The reactions from visitors are overwhelmingly positive, with many praising the gallery’s unique ability to make art accessible to everyone.  The seating areas scattered throughout the gallery are thoughtfully placed, offering a chance to sit and reflect on the art while enjoying a cup of coffee or a glass of wine. It’s a place where conversations naturally flow, as the art sparks dialogue and thought. Couples, families, and solo visitors all find something to appreciate in this well-balanced mix of visual, auditory, and culinary experiences.  The gallery’s dedication to detail, from the layout of the exhibits to the menu in the café, speaks volumes about their passion for art and hospitality. Visitors often leave glowing reviews about how the gallery exceeded their expectations, not just with the art but with the entire experience. It’s more than just a gallery; it’s a cultural hub where creativity, conversation, and cuisine come together seamlessly. This space truly stands out for its ability to nourish both the body and soul. || Very Good Vibe Indeed. They have art event once a month approx.
